--!strict

-- Data that keeps itself consistent: bundles normalize a group of fields together, reactions
-- write one thing when another changes, derived fields are computed on read. Bundles and
-- reactions run inside the triggering transaction, so guards see their writes and a
-- rejection undoes them too

local Document = require("../Matrix/Document")
local Path = require("../Matrix/Path")
local Transaction = require("../Matrix/Transaction")
local Tree = require("../Matrix/Tree")

type Path = Path.Path
type PathLike = Path.PathLike
type Transaction = Transaction.Transaction

export type Bundle = {
	kind: "bundle",
	name: string,
	fields: { Path },
	normalize: (tx: Transaction) -> (),
}

export type Reaction = {
	kind: "reaction",
	name: string,
	deps: { Path },
	writes: { Path },
	run: (tx: Transaction) -> (),
}

export type Derived = {
	kind: "derived",
	name: string,
	deps: { Path },
	compute: (state: unknown) -> unknown,
}

export type BundleOptions = {
	name: string?,
}

export type ReactionOptions = {
	name: string?,
	-- every path the reaction may write. Required, cycle detection runs off this
	writes: { PathLike },
}

export type SetOptions = {
	bundles: { Bundle }?,
	reactions: { Reaction }?,
	derived: { Derived }?,
	-- max rounds of bundles and reactions per transaction, default 8
	maxDepth: number?,
}

local Facet = {}

local DEFAULT_MAX_DEPTH = 8

local function parseAll(paths: { PathLike }, what: string): { Path }
	assert(type(paths) == "table" and #paths > 0, `{what} needs at least one path`)
	local parsed = {}
	for _, path in paths do
		table.insert(parsed, table.freeze(Path.parse(path)))
	end
	return table.freeze(parsed)
end

local function describePaths(paths: { Path }): string
	local parts = {}
	for _, path in paths do
		table.insert(parts, Path.format(path))
	end
	return table.concat(parts, ", ")
end

local function overlaps(a: { Path }, b: { Path }): boolean
	for _, left in a do
		for _, right in b do
			if Path.related(left, right) then
				return true
			end
		end
	end
	return false
end

-- Builders

--[=[
	A group of fields kept consistent by one function. It runs whenever any of the fields changes,
	and may only write those fields

	@within Geode
	@param fields { PathLike }
	@param normalize (tx: Transaction) -> ()
	@param options BundleOptions?
	@return Bundle

	```lua
	local progress = Geode.bundle({ "xp", "level" }, function(tx)
		local xp, level = tx:get("xp"), tx:get("level")
		while xp >= level * 100 do
			xp -= level * 100
			level += 1
		end
		tx:set("xp", xp)
		tx:set("level", level)
	end)
	```
]=]
function Facet.bundle(
	fields: { PathLike },
	normalize: (tx: Transaction) -> (),
	options: BundleOptions?
): Bundle
	local parsed = parseAll(fields, "a bundle")
	assert(type(normalize) == "function", "a bundle needs a normalize function")
	return table.freeze({
		kind = "bundle" :: "bundle",
		name = options and options.name or `bundle({describePaths(parsed)})`,
		fields = parsed,
		normalize = normalize,
	})
end

--[=[
	Writes `writes` whenever something in `deps` changes, inside the same transaction

	@within Geode
	@param deps { PathLike }
	@param run (tx: Transaction) -> ()
	@param options ReactionOptions
	@return Reaction

	```lua
	Geode.react({ "level" }, function(tx)
		tx:increment("coins", 50)
	end, { writes = { "coins" } })
	```
]=]
function Facet.react(
	deps: { PathLike },
	run: (tx: Transaction) -> (),
	options: ReactionOptions
): Reaction
	local parsedDeps = parseAll(deps, "a reaction")
	assert(type(run) == "function", "a reaction needs a function to run")
	assert(
		options and options.writes,
		"a reaction has to declare the paths it writes, so cycles can be found before anything runs"
	)
	local parsedWrites = parseAll(options.writes, "a reaction's writes")
	return table.freeze({
		kind = "reaction" :: "reaction",
		name = options.name
			or `reaction({describePaths(parsedDeps)} -> {describePaths(parsedWrites)})`,
		deps = parsedDeps,
		writes = parsedWrites,
		run = run,
	})
end

--[=[
	A top level field computed from `deps` when read. It's never stored or written, and only
	recomputes when a dependency changed

	@within Geode
	@param name string
	@param deps { PathLike }
	@param compute (state: unknown) -> unknown
	@return Derived
]=]
function Facet.derive(
	name: string,
	deps: { PathLike },
	compute: (state: unknown) -> unknown
): Derived
	assert(type(name) == "string" and name ~= "", "a derived field needs a name")
	assert(not string.find(name, ".", 1, true), "a derived field name can't contain dots")
	assert(type(compute) == "function", "a derived field needs a compute function")
	return table.freeze({
		kind = "derived" :: "derived",
		name = name,
		deps = parseAll(deps, "a derived field"),
		compute = compute,
	})
end

-- Graph

type Node = {
	name: string,
	reads: { Path },
	writes: { Path },
	reaction: Reaction?,
}

-- Orders reactions so each runs after everything it depends on, and errors on cycles. Bundles
-- are nodes too (they read and write their own fields), so a loop through one is caught
local function order(bundles: { Bundle }, reactions: { Reaction }): { Reaction }
	local nodes: { Node } = {}
	for _, bundle in bundles do
		table.insert(
			nodes,
			{ name = bundle.name, reads = bundle.fields, writes = bundle.fields, reaction = nil }
		)
	end
	for _, reaction in reactions do
		table.insert(nodes, {
			name = reaction.name,
			reads = reaction.deps,
			writes = reaction.writes,
			reaction = reaction,
		})
	end

	local edges: { [Node]: { Node } } = {}
	local incoming: { [Node]: number } = {}
	for _, node in nodes do
		edges[node] = {}
		incoming[node] = 0
	end
	for _, from in nodes do
		for _, to in nodes do
			local isBundleItself = from == to and from.reaction == nil
			if not isBundleItself and overlaps(from.writes, to.reads) then
				if from == to then
					error(`{from.name} writes a path it depends on, which would trigger itself`, 0)
				end
				table.insert(edges[from], to)
				incoming[to] += 1
			end
		end
	end

	local ready = {}
	for _, node in nodes do
		if incoming[node] == 0 then
			table.insert(ready, node)
		end
	end
	local sorted: { Reaction } = {}
	local visited = 0
	while #ready > 0 do
		local node = table.remove(ready, 1) :: Node
		visited += 1
		if node.reaction then
			table.insert(sorted, node.reaction)
		end
		for _, next in edges[node] do
			incoming[next] -= 1
			if incoming[next] == 0 then
				table.insert(ready, next)
			end
		end
	end

	if visited < #nodes then
		local stuck = {}
		for _, node in nodes do
			if incoming[node] > 0 then
				table.insert(stuck, node.name)
			end
		end
		table.sort(stuck)
		error(`bundles and reactions form a cycle through {table.concat(stuck, ", ")}`, 0)
	end
	return sorted
end

--// facet sets

type Fields = {
	order: { Reaction },
	_bundles: { Bundle },
	_derived: { Derived },
	_maxDepth: number,
}

--[=[
	@class FacetSet

	Bundles, reactions and derived fields checked together. Made with `Geode.Raw.facets`
]=]
local FacetSet = {}
FacetSet.__index = FacetSet

export type FacetSet = typeof(setmetatable({} :: Fields, FacetSet))

--[=[
	Validates bundles and reactions together and fixes their run order. Cycles, and reactions
	that trigger themselves, error here rather than at runtime

	@within FacetSet
	@param options FacetSetOptions
	@return FacetSet
]=]
function Facet.set(options: SetOptions): FacetSet
	local bundles: { Bundle } = if options.bundles then options.bundles else {}
	local reactions: { Reaction } = if options.reactions then options.reactions else {}
	local derived: { Derived } = if options.derived then options.derived else {}

	local names: { [string]: boolean } = {}
	for _, item in derived do
		assert(not names[item.name], `two derived fields are named {item.name}`)
		names[item.name] = true
	end

	local self: Fields = {
		order = table.freeze(order(bundles, reactions)),
		_bundles = table.clone(bundles),
		_derived = table.clone(derived),
		_maxDepth = options.maxDepth or DEFAULT_MAX_DEPTH,
	}
	assert(self._maxDepth >= 1, "maxDepth must be at least 1")
	return setmetatable(self, FacetSet)
end

local function touches(changes: { Tree.DiffEntry }, paths: { Path }): boolean
	for _, entry in changes do
		for _, path in paths do
			if Path.related(entry.path, path) then
				return true
			end
		end
	end
	return false
end

-- Runs one bundle or reaction and returns what it changed. Writes outside what it may write are
-- refused, which keeps the definition time cycle check honest
local function step(
	tx: Transaction,
	name: string,
	allowed: { Path },
	writer: Transaction.SourceKind,
	body: (tx: Transaction) -> ()
): { Tree.DiffEntry }
	local before = tx:get()
	body(tx)
	local changes = Tree.diff(before, tx:get())
	for _, entry in changes do
		local inside = false
		for _, path in allowed do
			if Path.startsWith(entry.path, path) then
				inside = true
				break
			end
		end
		if not inside then
			Transaction.fail(
				"error",
				`{name} wrote {Path.format(entry.path)}, which isn't among the paths it may write`
			)
		end
		tx:markWriter(Path.format(entry.path), writer)
	end
	return changes
end

local function append(target: { Tree.DiffEntry }, source: { Tree.DiffEntry })
	table.move(source, 1, #source, #target + 1, target)
end

--[=[
	The pipeline stage. Round one runs bundles touched by the caller's changes, then reactions in
	order. Later rounds only happen when reactions touched bundle members: those bundles normalize
	again and reactions see just their new writes
]=]
function FacetSet.stage(self: FacetSet): (tx: Transaction) -> ()
	return function(tx: Transaction)
		local pending = tx:diff()
		for _, entry in pending do
			tx:markWriter(Path.format(entry.path), tx.source.kind)
		end

		local round = 0
		local triggers = pending
		while true do
			round += 1
			if round > self._maxDepth then
				Transaction.fail(
					"error",
					`bundles and reactions didn't settle within {self._maxDepth} rounds`
				)
			end

			local bundleWrites: { Tree.DiffEntry } = {}
			for _, bundle in self._bundles do
				if touches(pending, bundle.fields) then
					append(
						bundleWrites,
						step(tx, bundle.name, bundle.fields, "bundle", bundle.normalize)
					)
				end
			end
			if round > 1 then
				if #bundleWrites == 0 then
					break
				end
				triggers = {}
			end
			append(triggers, bundleWrites)

			local reactionWrites: { Tree.DiffEntry } = {}
			for _, reaction in self.order do
				if touches(triggers, reaction.deps) then
					local changes =
						step(tx, reaction.name, reaction.writes, "reaction", reaction.run)
					append(triggers, changes)
					append(reactionWrites, changes)
				end
			end

			if #reactionWrites == 0 then
				break
			end
			pending = reactionWrites
		end
	end
end

-- Only recomputes when an input changed. Structural sharing means an unchanged input is the
-- very same value, so a reference compare is enough
local function cached(derived: Derived): (root: unknown) -> unknown
	local lastInputs: { unknown }? = nil
	local lastValue: unknown = nil
	return function(root: unknown): unknown
		local inputs = {}
		for index, dep in derived.deps do
			inputs[index] = Tree.get(root, dep)
		end
		if lastInputs then
			local same = true
			for index, value in inputs do
				if lastInputs[index] ~= value then
					same = false
					break
				end
			end
			if same then
				return lastValue
			end
		end
		lastInputs = inputs
		lastValue = Tree.adopt(derived.compute(root))
		return lastValue
	end
end

--[=[
	Adds the stage and the derived fields to a document. Attach it before any guard set so the
	guards see what bundles and reactions wrote
]=]
function FacetSet.attach(self: FacetSet, document: Document.Document)
	for _, derived in self._derived do
		local deps: { PathLike } = {}
		for _, dep in derived.deps do
			table.insert(deps, dep)
		end
		document:addDerived(derived.name, deps, cached(derived))
	end
	if #self._bundles > 0 or #self.order > 0 then
		document:addStage(self:stage())
	end
end

return Facet

-- MaterialService's overrides and variant lookup, and the defaults of the
-- material classes (M4 step 5). Everything changed is put back. Members
-- needing plugin capability (MaterialVariant.BaseMaterial's setter) are left
-- out: the recorder runs with it, game scripts don't.
local ms = game:GetService("MaterialService")
log("Plastic", ms:GetBaseMaterialOverride(Enum.Material.Plastic))
log("Neon", pcall(function()
	return ms:GetBaseMaterialOverride(Enum.Material.Neon)
end))
log("set Neon", pcall(function()
	ms:SetBaseMaterialOverride(Enum.Material.Neon, "X")
end))
log("by name", pcall(function()
	return ms:GetBaseMaterialOverride("Wood")
end))
local before = ms:GetBaseMaterialOverride(Enum.Material.Wood)
ms:SetBaseMaterialOverride(Enum.Material.Wood, "NoSuchVariant")
log("Wood", ms:GetBaseMaterialOverride(Enum.Material.Wood))
ms:SetBaseMaterialOverride(Enum.Material.Wood, "")
log("Wood empty", string.format("%q", ms:GetBaseMaterialOverride(Enum.Material.Wood)))
ms:SetBaseMaterialOverride(Enum.Material.Wood, before)

local folder = Instance.new("Folder")
local v = Instance.new("MaterialVariant")
v.Name = "RookCaseVariant"
v.Parent = folder
log("defaults", v.BaseMaterial, v.StudsPerTile, v.MaterialPattern)

--!strict

-- Cross-server matchmaking. Tickets sit in a MemoryStore sorted map ordered by rating, and any
-- server can add or cancel them. One server per mode and region, elected with a lock, groups
-- them into matches each tick. Claims are atomic updates that only succeed on an unclaimed
-- ticket, so two matchers can never put the same player in two matches

local Premades = require("../Moonstone/Premades")
local RealServices = require("../Quartz/Real/Services")
local VeinBridge = require("../Vein/Bridge")
local Registry = require("../Vein/Registry")
local Scheduler = require("../Quartz/Scheduler")
local Types = require("../Quartz/Types")

export type Band = {
	-- Rating gap allowed right away. Defaults to 100
	start: number?,
	-- How much the band grows each second a ticket waits. Defaults to 10
	widenPerSecond: number?,
	-- The widest it gets. Defaults to 1000
	max: number?,
}

export type Options = {
	name: string,
	placeId: number,
	-- Players per match. Parties count with all their members and are never split
	matchSize: number,
	mode: string?,
	region: string?,
	band: Band?,
	-- Seconds a ticket waits before it expires. Defaults to 300
	ticketTtl: number?,
	-- Seconds between matching passes, default 2
	tick: number?,
	-- Seconds the elected matcher's lock lasts without renewal. Defaults to 10
	lease: number?,
	-- One matcher per mode and region, on by default. Off lets every server match, which
	-- is still safe, just costs more
	elect: boolean?,
	onMatch: ((match: Match) -> ())?,
	services: Types.Services?,
	scheduler: Scheduler.Scheduler?,
	reportError: ((message: string) -> ())?,
}

export type Ticket = {
	id: string,
	players: { number },
	rating: number,
	createdAt: number,
	matchId: string?,
	reservedCode: string?,
	-- set by cancel. The ticket lingers for a second and must not be matched in that time
	cancelled: boolean?,
}

export type Match = {
	id: string,
	placeId: number,
	reservedCode: string,
	players: { number },
	tickets: { string },
}

export type Status = {
	state: "waiting" | "matched" | "gone",
	ticket: Ticket?,
}

type Fields = {
	name: string,
	mode: string,
	region: string,
	_services: Types.Services,
	_scheduler: Scheduler.Scheduler,
	_map: Types.SortedMap,
	_placeId: number,
	_matchSize: number,
	_band: { start: number, widenPerSecond: number, max: number },
	_ticketTtl: number,
	_tick: number,
	_elect: boolean,
	_mutex: Premades.Mutex,
	_lock: Premades.Lock?,
	_running: boolean,
	-- bumped on every start so a loop left over from a quick stop/start exits by itself
	_loop: number,
	_onMatch: ((match: Match) -> ())?,
	_report: (message: string) -> (),
	_handle: Registry.Handle,
}

--[=[
	@class Matchmaker

	Matchmaking across servers. Made with `Geode.Matchmaker.new`
]=]
local Matchmaker = {}
Matchmaker.__index = Matchmaker

export type Matchmaker = typeof(setmetatable({} :: Fields, Matchmaker))

-- GetRangeAsync max
local PAGE = 200
local MAX_PAGES = 5

--[=[
	Creates a matchmaker for one mode and region. Call `start` on every server that should take
	part in electing the matcher

	@within Matchmaker
	@param options MatchmakerOptions
	@return Matchmaker
]=]
function Matchmaker.new(options: Options): Matchmaker
	assert(type(options.name) == "string" and options.name ~= "", "a matchmaker needs a name")
	assert(
		options.matchSize >= 2 and options.matchSize % 1 == 0,
		"matchSize must be a whole number of at least 2"
	)
	local services = options.services or RealServices.live()
	VeinBridge.ensure(services)
	local scheduler = options.scheduler
		or Scheduler.new({ clock = services.clock, budget = services.budget })
	local mode = options.mode or "default"
	local region = options.region or "global"
	local band: Band = options.band or {}
	local self = setmetatable(
		{
			name = options.name,
			mode = mode,
			region = region,
			_services = services,
			_scheduler = scheduler,
			_map = services.sortedMap(`geode_mm_{options.name}_{mode}_{region}`),
			_placeId = options.placeId,
			_matchSize = options.matchSize,
			_band = {
				start = band.start or 100,
				widenPerSecond = band.widenPerSecond or 10,
				max = band.max or 1000,
			},
			_ticketTtl = options.ticketTtl or 300,
			_tick = options.tick or 2,
			_elect = options.elect ~= false,
			_mutex = Premades.mutex(`matchmaker_{options.name}`, {
				services = services,
				scheduler = scheduler,
				lease = options.lease or 10,
			}),
			_lock = nil,
			_running = false,
			_loop = 0,
			_onMatch = options.onMatch,
			_report = options.reportError or function(message: string)
				warn(message)
			end,
			_handle = nil :: any,
		} :: Fields,
		Matchmaker
	)
	self._handle = Registry.register("matchmaker", `{options.name}/{mode}/{region}`, function()
		return { matcher = self:isMatcher() }
	end)
	return self
end

-- Tickets

--[=[
	Queues players as a single ticket and returns its id. A party is one ticket, so it always
	lands in the same match
]=]
function Matchmaker.enqueue(
	self: Matchmaker,
	players: { number },
	rating: number
): Types.Result<string>
	assert(
		#players >= 1 and #players <= self._matchSize,
		"a ticket holds between 1 and matchSize players"
	)
	local id = self._services.guid()
	local ticket: Ticket = {
		id = id,
		players = table.clone(players),
		rating = rating,
		createdAt = self._services.clock:now(),
		matchId = nil,
		reservedCode = nil,
	}
	local result = self._scheduler:submit({
		priority = "save",
		run = function()
			return self._map:set(id, ticket, self._ticketTtl, rating)
		end,
	})
	if not result.ok then
		return { ok = false, error = result.error }
	end
	return { ok = true, value = id }
end

--[=[
	Takes a ticket out of the queue. Returns false when it was already matched or gone
]=]
function Matchmaker.cancel(self: Matchmaker, ticketId: string): Types.Result<boolean>
	local cancelled = false
	local result = self._scheduler:submit({
		priority = "save",
		run = function()
			return self._map:update(ticketId, function(current: unknown, sortKey: Types.SortKey?)
				cancelled = false
				if type(current) ~= "table" or (current :: Ticket).matchId ~= nil then
					return nil, nil
				end
				cancelled = true
				-- Mark it and let it expire. Removing it now could race a claim
				-- that's already reading it, and the mark makes every claim refuse it
				local ticket = table.clone(current :: Ticket)
				ticket.cancelled = true
				return ticket, sortKey
			end, 1)
		end,
	})
	if not result.ok then
		return { ok = false, error = result.error }
	end
	return { ok = true, value = cancelled }
end

--[=[
	Where a ticket stands: still waiting, matched with a reserved server, or gone because it was
	cancelled or expired
]=]
function Matchmaker.status(self: Matchmaker, ticketId: string): Types.Result<Status>
	local result = self._scheduler:submit({
		priority = "read",
		run = function()
			return self._map:get(ticketId)
		end,
	})
	if not result.ok then
		return { ok = false, error = result.error }
	end
	local entry = result.value
	if entry == nil or type(entry.value) ~= "table" or (entry.value :: Ticket).cancelled then
		return { ok = true, value = { state = "gone", ticket = nil } }
	end
	local ticket = entry.value :: Ticket
	return {
		ok = true,
		value = { state = if ticket.matchId then "matched" else "waiting", ticket = ticket },
	}
end

--[=[
	Teleports this server's players from a matched ticket to their reserved server
]=]
function Matchmaker.teleport(
	self: Matchmaker,
	ticket: Ticket,
	players: { unknown }
): Types.Result<nil>
	assert(ticket.reservedCode, "the ticket isn't matched yet")
	return self._services.teleport:teleport(self._placeId, players, {
		reservedServerCode = ticket.reservedCode,
		data = { matchId = ticket.matchId },
	})
end

-- Matching

function Matchmaker._bandFor(self: Matchmaker, waited: number): number
	local band = self._band
	return math.min(band.start + band.widenPerSecond * math.max(0, waited), band.max)
end

-- Groups waiting tickets, lowest rating first. Each group fills a match exactly
function Matchmaker._groups(self: Matchmaker, tickets: { Ticket }): { { Ticket } }
	local now = self._services.clock:now()
	local used: { [string]: boolean } = {}
	local groups = {}
	for index, anchor in tickets do
		if used[anchor.id] then
			continue
		end
		local band = self:_bandFor(now - anchor.createdAt)
		local group = { anchor }
		local size = #anchor.players
		for other = index + 1, #tickets do
			if size == self._matchSize then
				break
			end
			local candidate = tickets[other]
			if candidate.rating - anchor.rating > band then
				break
			end
			if not used[candidate.id] and size + #candidate.players <= self._matchSize then
				table.insert(group, candidate)
				size += #candidate.players
			end
		end
		if size == self._matchSize then
			for _, ticket in group do
				used[ticket.id] = true
			end
			table.insert(groups, group)
		end
	end
	return groups
end

-- All or nothing: claims every ticket in the group for one match, or none
function Matchmaker._claim(
	self: Matchmaker,
	group: { Ticket },
	matchId: string,
	code: string
): boolean
	local claimed: { string } = {}
	local function setMatch(
		ticketId: string,
		expected: string?,
		matchValue: string?,
		codeValue: string?
	): boolean
		local changed = false
		local result = self._scheduler:submit({
			priority = "load",
			run = function()
				return self._map:update(
					ticketId,
					function(current: unknown, sortKey: Types.SortKey?)
						changed = false
						if
							type(current) ~= "table"
							or (current :: Ticket).matchId ~= expected
							or (current :: Ticket).cancelled
						then
							return nil, nil
						end
						local ticket = table.clone(current :: Ticket)
						ticket.matchId = matchValue
						ticket.reservedCode = codeValue
						changed = true
						return ticket, sortKey
					end,
					self._ticketTtl
				)
			end,
		})
		return result.ok and changed
	end

	for _, ticket in group do
		if setMatch(ticket.id, nil, matchId, code) then
			table.insert(claimed, ticket.id)
		else
			-- Lost one: someone else took it or it's gone. Give back what this pass claimed
			for _, ticketId in claimed do
				setMatch(ticketId, matchId, nil, nil)
			end
			return false
		end
	end
	return true
end

--[=[
	Runs one matching pass and returns the matches it made. The elected matcher runs this every
	tick, so call it directly only in tests or custom loops
]=]
function Matchmaker.runOnce(self: Matchmaker): { Match }
	-- Matched tickets linger until they expire, so page past them. The bound carries key and
	-- sortKey both: a key-only bound ranks as "no sort key" (found this in testing)
	local tickets: { Ticket } = {}
	local lower: Types.SortedBound? = nil
	for _ = 1, MAX_PAGES do
		local bound = lower
		local range = self._scheduler:submit({
			priority = "read",
			run = function()
				return self._map:getRange({ count = PAGE, lower = bound })
			end,
		})
		if not range.ok then
			self._report(`matchmaker {self.name} couldn't read its queue: {range.error.message}`)
			return {}
		end
		for _, entry in range.value do
			local ticket = entry.value
			if
				type(ticket) == "table"
				and (ticket :: Ticket).matchId == nil
				and not (ticket :: Ticket).cancelled
			then
				table.insert(tickets, ticket :: Ticket)
			end
		end
		local last = range.value[#range.value]
		if #range.value < PAGE or #tickets >= PAGE or last == nil then
			break
		end
		lower = { key = last.key, sortKey = last.sortKey }
	end

	local matches = {}
	for _, group in self:_groups(tickets) do
		local reserved = self._services.teleport:reserveServer(self._placeId)
		if not reserved.ok then
			self._report(
				`matchmaker {self.name} couldn't reserve a server: {reserved.error.message}`
			)
			break
		end
		local matchId = self._services.guid()
		if self:_claim(group, matchId, reserved.value.code) then
			local match: Match = {
				id = matchId,
				placeId = self._placeId,
				reservedCode = reserved.value.code,
				players = {},
				tickets = {},
			}
			for _, ticket in group do
				table.insert(match.tickets, ticket.id)
				for _, userId in ticket.players do
					table.insert(match.players, userId)
				end
			end
			table.insert(matches, match)
			local onMatch = self._onMatch
			if onMatch then
				local ok, err = pcall(function()
					onMatch(match)
				end)
				if not ok then
					self._report(`onMatch handler error: {tostring(err)}`)
				end
			end
		end
	end
	return matches
end

--// matcher loop

--[=[
	Whether this server is the elected matcher right now
]=]
function Matchmaker.isMatcher(self: Matchmaker): boolean
	if not self._elect then
		return self._running
	end
	local lock = self._lock
	return lock ~= nil and lock:isHeld()
end

-- True when this server should match this tick. Keeps the role or tries to take it
function Matchmaker._elected(self: Matchmaker): boolean
	if not self._elect then
		return true
	end
	local lock = self._lock
	if lock and lock:isHeld() and lock:renew() then
		return true
	end
	self._lock = nil
	local acquired = self._mutex:acquire(`{self.mode}:{self.region}`)
	if acquired.ok and acquired.value then
		self._lock = acquired.value
		return true
	end
	return false
end

--[=[
	Takes part in matching: tries to become the matcher every tick, and matches while it is.
	When the matcher's server dies, its lock runs out and another server takes over
]=]
function Matchmaker.start(self: Matchmaker)
	if self._running then
		return
	end
	self._running = true
	self._loop += 1
	local loop = self._loop
	local clock = self._services.clock
	clock:spawn(function()
		while self._running and self._loop == loop do
			if self:_elected() then
				self:runOnce()
			end
			clock:wait(self._tick)
		end
	end)
end

--[=[
	Stops taking part in matching and gives up the matcher lock if this server held it

	@within Matchmaker
]=]
function Matchmaker.stop(self: Matchmaker)
	self._running = false
	local lock = self._lock
	self._lock = nil
	if lock then
		self._services.clock:spawn(function()
			lock:release()
		end)
	end
end

--[=[
	Stops it and drops it from the registry that tooling reads

	@within Matchmaker
]=]
function Matchmaker.destroy(self: Matchmaker)
	self:stop()
	self._handle:unregister()
	self._mutex:destroy()
end

return Matchmaker

end))

    return mp.InitialSize
end))

log("set MeshSize", pcall(function()
    mp.MeshSize = Vector3.one
end))

--!strict
--!nolint DeprecatedApi
--[=[
	Benchmark helpers.

	measure(run, iterations, trials)
		Calls run(iterations) once to warm up, then `trials` more times,
		yielding between trials. Returns the median, fastest and slowest
		time per iteration in microseconds.

	bytesPerObject(build, count, trials)
		Builds `count` objects (build(count) must return something that
		keeps them alive) many times and reports Luau heap growth in bytes
		per object. Garbage collection running during a build can only make
		a sample SMALLER (it frees unrelated garbage), so the method uses
		many small builds and reports the 80th percentile: the upper
		samples are the uninterrupted ones, and the very top is dropped in
		case something else allocated. Run it in an idle Edit session.
		In testing this gave identical results across repeated rounds,
		whereas the median of large builds did not.

	ratioInterval(a, b, rng)
		For two lists of per-run results (a = this build, b = baseline),
		returns median(a) / median(b) and a 95% bootstrap confidence
		interval for that ratio: both lists are resampled with replacement
		2,000 times. A change whose interval doesn't include 1 is unlikely
		to be noise.

	leakCheck(build, timeoutSeconds)
		Proves that objects become collectable once released. build()
		returns (objects, release): every object is put in a weak-keyed
		table, release() is called, all strong references are dropped, and
		the check waits until the garbage collector has removed them.
		Roblox cannot force a collection, so the check creates throwaway
		garbage to keep the collector running. Returns how many objects are
		still alive when it finishes (0 means no leak) and how long it took.
]=]

local Bench = {}

-- Heap size in KB. collectgarbage("count") has sub-KB precision (gcinfo()
-- returns whole KB, hence the lint exception above); gcinfo() is the fallback.
local function heapKB(): number
	local ok, value = pcall(collectgarbage :: any, "count")
	if ok and type(value) == "number" then
		return value
	end
	return gcinfo()
end
Bench.heapKB = heapKB

local function median(values: { number }): number
	local sorted = table.clone(values)
	table.sort(sorted)
	local count = #sorted
	if count % 2 == 1 then
		return sorted[(count + 1) // 2]
	end
	return (sorted[count // 2] + sorted[count // 2 + 1]) / 2
end
Bench.median = median

function Bench.measure(run: (iterations: number) -> (), iterations: number, trials: number?): (number, number, number)
	local count = trials or 5
	run(math.max(1, iterations // 10)) -- warm-up
	task.wait()
	local samples = table.create(count)
	for _ = 1, count do
		local started = os.clock()
		run(iterations)
		local elapsed = os.clock() - started
		table.insert(samples, elapsed / iterations * 1e6)
		task.wait()
	end
	table.sort(samples)
	return samples[(count + 1) // 2], samples[1], samples[count]
end

function Bench.bytesPerObject(build: (count: number) -> any, count: number, trials: number?): number
	local runs = trials or 21
	local samples = table.create(runs)
	for _ = 1, runs do
		task.wait()
		local before = heapKB()
		local _keep = build(count)
		local after = heapKB()
		table.insert(samples, (after - before) * 1024 / count)
		_keep = nil
	end
	table.sort(samples)
	return math.max(0, samples[math.ceil(runs * 0.8)])
end

function Bench.ratioInterval(a: { number }, b: { number }, rng: Random): (number, number, number)
	local ratio = median(a) / median(b)
	local samples = table.create(2000)
	local resampledA, resampledB = table.create(#a), table.create(#b)
	for index = 1, 2000 do
		for slot = 1, #a do
			resampledA[slot] = a[rng:NextInteger(1, #a)]
		end
		for slot = 1, #b do
			resampledB[slot] = b[rng:NextInteger(1, #b)]
		end
		samples[index] = median(resampledA) / median(resampledB)
	end
	table.sort(samples)
	return ratio, samples[50], samples[1951]
end

function Bench.leakCheck(build: () -> ({ any }, () -> ()), timeoutSeconds: number?): (number, number)
	local tracked: { [any]: true } = setmetatable({} :: any, { __mode = "k" })
	-- Built and released on a thread that then finishes. While this thread
	-- waits for the collector, stale slots of its own stack (the loop
	-- variable holds the last object) still count as references, so building
	-- here could keep one object alive.
	local done, ok, err = false, true, nil
	task.spawn(function()
		ok, err = pcall(function()
			local objects, release = build()
			for _, object in objects do
				tracked[object] = true
			end
			release()
		end)
		done = true
	end)
	while not done do
		task.wait()
	end
	if not ok then
		error(err, 0)
	end

	local function alive(): number
		local count = 0
		for _ in tracked do
			count += 1
		end
		return count
	end

	local started = os.clock()
	local deadline = started + (timeoutSeconds or 10)
	while alive() > 0 and os.clock() < deadline do
		-- Throwaway allocations keep the incremental collector running.
		for _ = 1, 20000 do
			local _ = { 1, 2, 3 }
		end
		task.wait()
	end
	return alive(), os.clock() - started
end

return Bench

--!nonstrict
--!nolint DeprecatedApi
--[=[
	Constella benchmarks. Run from the Studio command bar (Edit mode):

	```lua
	print(require(game.ServerScriptService.ConstellaBenchmarks.RunBenchmarks)())
	print(require(game.ServerScriptService.ConstellaBenchmarks.RunBenchmarks)({ Runs = 7 }))
	-- Only some groups (speed, memory and leak cases alike):
	print(require(game.ServerScriptService.ConstellaBenchmarks.RunBenchmarks)({ Groups = { "Signal" } }))
	```

	Optional comparisons: put these ModuleScripts in ServerStorage.BenchmarkLibs
	(CI downloads pinned versions; see ci.yml):
	- "Signal"      - sleitnick/signal (GoodSignal-style)
	- "LemonSignal" - Data-Oriented-House/LemonSignal
	- "Trove"       - sleitnick/trove
	- "Janitor"     - howmanysmall/Janitor
	- "Promise"     - evaera/roblox-lua-promise
	Missing libraries are skipped. Returns a Markdown report.

	A/B comparisons: pass several builds of the package, for example the
	current code and the last release. Every case runs for every build
	back to back inside each run, and every other run reverses their order,
	so the builds are measured under the same conditions. Implementation
	names then end in "[name]", and the first build is compared with the
	second: median ratio, a 95% bootstrap confidence interval, and a
	REGRESSION line for any case that is more than 10% slower with the
	interval's lower end above +5%.

	```lua
	RunBenchmarks({
		Runs = 7,
		Packages = {
			{ Name = "this build", Module = ReplicatedStorage.Packages.Constella },
			{ Name = "baseline", Module = ReplicatedStorage.Packages.ConstellaBaseline },
		},
	})
	```

	Method
	- Speed: the whole suite runs `Runs` times (default 5). Within a run,
	  each case is the median of 5 timed trials. The report shows the
	  median across runs, the best and worst run, and then every run's
	  result in the order the runs happened.
	- Memory: bytes per object, 80th percentile of many builds (see
	  Bench.bytesPerObject for why).
	- Bandwidth: estimated bytes sent per Replication update, measured with
	  Network.Payload (the same estimate Network uses for its limits).
	- Leaks: objects are released while their owner stays alive, then the
	  check waits for the garbage collector to free them (see Bench.luau).
]=]

local CollectionService = game:GetService("CollectionService")
local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage")
local ServerStorage = game:GetService("ServerStorage")

local Bench = require(script.Parent.Bench)

local function noop() end

local function one()
	return 1
end

local function traceback(err)
	return debug.traceback(tostring(err), 2)
end

type Package = { Name: string?, Module: ModuleScript }

-- A 40-item inventory, the shape a Replication share often has.
local function inventory(coins: number)
	local items = table.create(40)
	for index = 1, 40 do
		items[index] = { Id = "Item" .. index, Count = index }
	end
	return { Coins = coins, Items = items }
end

local REGRESSION_RATIO, REGRESSION_LOWER = 1.10, 1.05

-- Memory cases by group, for the Groups option.
local MEMORY_GROUPS = {
	["Connected listener"] = "Signal",
	["Tracked function"] = "Cleanup",
	["Resolved promise"] = "Promise",
	["Pending promise from Then"] = "Promise",
}

return function(options: { Runs: number?, Packages: { Package }?, Groups: { string }? }?): string
	local runs = (options and options.Runs) or 5
	-- nil runs every group.
	local groups: { [string]: boolean }? = nil
	if options and options.Groups then
		groups = {}
		for _, group in options.Groups do
			(groups :: any)[group] = true
		end
	end
	local function wants(group: string): boolean
		return groups == nil or groups[group] == true
	end
	local packages: { Package } = (options and options.Packages)
		or { { Module = ReplicatedStorage:WaitForChild("Packages"):WaitForChild("Constella") } }
	local libs = ServerStorage:FindFirstChild("BenchmarkLibs")
	local function lib(name: string): any
		local module = libs and libs:FindFirstChild(name)
		return if module then require(module :: any) else nil
	end
	local OtherSignal = lib("Signal")
	local LemonSignal = lib("LemonSignal")
	local Trove = lib("Trove")
	local Janitor = lib("Janitor")
	local OtherPromise = lib("Promise")

	-- Speed cases ----------------------------------------------------------
	local cases: { any } = {}
	local currentBuild: number? = nil
	local function case(group, name, implementation, iterations, run)
		if not wants(group) then
			return
		end
		table.insert(cases, {
			group = group,
			name = name,
			implementation = implementation,
			iterations = iterations,
			run = run,
			samples = {},
			build = currentBuild,
		})
	end

	-- Everything created for the cases, destroyed after the speed runs.
	local fixtures: { any } = {}
	local function keep(object: any): any
		table.insert(fixtures, object)
		return object
	end

	local bindable = keep(Instance.new("BindableEvent"))
	local template = Instance.new("Part")
	template.Anchored = true
	keep(template)
	local folder = keep(Instance.new("Folder"))
	folder.Parent = workspace
	local player = { Name = "Bench" }

	local entries = {}
	for index = 1, 100 do
		entries[index] = { Value = index, Weight = index }
	end
	local rng = Random.new(1)

	-- Distinct functions to hand to cleanup managers. (Adding the same
	-- function many times isn't a fair test: Janitor keys entries by the
	-- object, so it would keep just one.)
	local distinct = table.create(5000)
	for index = 1, 5000 do
		distinct[index] = function()
			return index
		end
	end

	local function plain(fn)
		return fn
	end
	local function isolated(fn)
		return function(...)
			xpcall(fn, traceback, ...)
		end
	end

	local function signalCases(label, new, wrap)
		case("Signal", "Connect + Disconnect", label, 20000, function(n)
			local signal = new()
			for _ = 1, n do
				signal:Connect(noop):Disconnect()
			end
		end)
		case("Signal", "Fire, 1 listener", label, 20000, function(n)
			local signal = new()
			signal:Connect(wrap(noop))
			for _ = 1, n do
				signal:Fire(1, 2)
			end
		end)
		case("Signal", "Fire, 10 listeners", label, 5000, function(n)
			local signal = new()
			for _ = 1, 10 do
				signal:Connect(wrap(noop))
			end
			for _ = 1, n do
				signal:Fire(1, 2)
			end
		end)
		-- Larger counts show whether the cost per listener stays constant.
		for _, listeners in { 100, 1000 } do
			case("Signal", ("Fire, %d listeners"):format(listeners), label, 50000 // listeners, function(n)
				local signal = new()
				for _ = 1, listeners do
					signal:Connect(wrap(noop))
				end
				for _ = 1, n do
					signal:Fire(1, 2)
				end
			end)
		end
	end

	-- `adapter` hides the API differences: new(), addFunction(manager, fn),
	-- addConnection(manager, event, fn), clean(manager).
	local function cleanupCases(label, adapter)
		case("Cleanup", "Add + Clean 100 functions", label, 300, function(n)
			for _ = 1, n do
				local manager = adapter.new()
				for index = 1, 100 do
					adapter.addFunction(manager, distinct[index])
				end
				adapter.clean(manager)
			end
		end)
		case("Cleanup", "Connect + Clean 100 RBXScriptConnections", label, 100, function(n)
			for _ = 1, n do
				local manager = adapter.new()
				for _ = 1, 100 do
					adapter.addConnection(manager, bindable.Event, noop)
				end
				adapter.clean(manager)
			end
		end)
	end

	-- `adapter`: resolve(value), new(executor), andThen(promise, fn), await(promise)
	local function promiseCases(label, adapter)
		case("Promise", "`resolve` + `Then` + `Await`", label, 5000, function(n)
			for _ = 1, n do
				adapter.await(adapter.andThen(adapter.resolve(1), one))
			end
		end)
		case("Promise", "Chain 10 `Then`s, then resolve", label, 1000, function(n)
			for _ = 1, n do
				local resolve
				local promise = adapter.new(function(done)
					resolve = done
				end)
				for _ = 1, 10 do
					promise = adapter.andThen(promise, one)
				end
				resolve(1)
			end
		end)
	end

	-- Every case that measures Constella, for one build of the package.
	local function constellaCases(Constella, suffix, buildIndex)
		-- Constella always isolates listener errors (xpcall + OnError).
		signalCases("Constella.Signal" .. suffix, Constella.Signal.new, plain)
		cleanupCases("Constella.Cleanup" .. suffix, {
			new = Constella.Cleanup.new,
			addFunction = function(manager, fn)
				manager:Add(fn)
			end,
			addConnection = function(manager, event, fn)
				manager:Connect(event, fn)
			end,
			clean = function(manager)
				manager:Clean()
			end,
		})

		case("Pool", "Spawn + despawn a Part", "Constella.Pool" .. suffix, 2000, function(n)
			local pool = Constella.Pool.instances(template, { MaxIdle = 16 })
			for _ = 1, n do
				local part = pool:Acquire()
				part.Parent = folder
				pool:Release(part)
			end
			pool:Destroy()
		end)

		local Network = Constella.Network
		local Check = Network.Check
		local server = keep(Network.Server.new("Benchmark", { Parent = Instance.new("Folder"), OnError = noop }))
		local schema = {
			Check.string(20),
			Check.integer(1, 99),
			Check.record({ Note = Check.optional(Check.string(50)) }),
		}
		local buy = server:Event("Buy", { Schema = schema, RateLimit = { Count = 1e9, Per = 1 } })
		buy:Connect(noop)
		case("Network", "Accept a valid request (all checks)", "Constella.Network" .. suffix, 20000, function(n)
			for _ = 1, n do
				buy:_receive(player, "Sword", 2, { Note = "gift" })
			end
		end)
		case("Network", "Reject a forged request", "Constella.Network" .. suffix, 20000, function(n)
			for _ = 1, n do
				buy:_receive(player, "Sword", 0 / 0, { Admin = true })
			end
		end)

		-- The same endpoint created from a contract (0.4.0). It must cost the
		-- same: at runtime it is the same endpoint behind the same gates.
		local hasContracts = pcall(function()
			return Network.Contract
		end)
		if hasContracts then
			local Contract = Network.Contract
			local shop = Contract.define({
				Namespace = "BenchmarkContract",
				Buy = Contract.event(schema),
			})
			local contractServer =
				keep(Network.Server.new("BenchmarkContract", { Parent = Instance.new("Folder"), OnError = noop }))
			local contractBuy = contractServer:EventOf(shop.Buy, { RateLimit = { Count = 1e9, Per = 1 } })
			contractBuy:Connect(noop)
			case(
				"Network",
				"Accept a valid request (all checks)",
				"Constella.Network, contract endpoint" .. suffix,
				20000,
				function(n)
					for _ = 1, n do
						contractBuy:_receive(player, "Sword", 2, { Note = "gift" })
					end
				end
			)
		end

		local loot = Constella.Random.lootTable(entries)
		case(
			"Random",
			"Weighted roll, 100 entries",
			"`Random.choose` (validates every call)" .. suffix,
			5000,
			function(n)
				for _ = 1, n do
					Constella.Random.choose(entries, rng)
				end
			end
		)
		case("Random", "Weighted roll, 100 entries", "`lootTable:Roll` (precomputed)" .. suffix, 50000, function(n)
			for _ = 1, n do
				loot:Roll(rng)
			end
		end)

		local State = Constella.State
		case("State", "Set with 1 subscriber", "Constella.State" .. suffix, 20000, function(n)
			local value = State.new(0)
			value:Subscribe(noop)
			for index = 1, n do
				value:Set(index)
			end
		end)
		case("State", "Set a source of a computed with 1 subscriber", "Constella.State" .. suffix, 20000, function(n)
			local a, b = State.new(0), State.new(1)
			local sum = State.computed({ a, b }, function(x, y)
				return x + y
			end)
			sum:Subscribe(noop)
			for index = 1, n do
				a:Set(index)
			end
			sum:Destroy()
		end)

		local Promise = Constella.Promise
		promiseCases("Constella.Promise" .. suffix, {
			resolve = Promise.resolve,
			new = Promise.new,
			andThen = function(promise, fn)
				return promise:Then(fn)
			end,
			await = function(promise)
				return promise:Await()
			end,
		})

		-- Zone: steady state (nothing enters or leaves), half the items inside.
		local Zone = Constella.Zone
		local pointZone =
			keep(Zone.new({ CFrame = CFrame.new(), Size = Vector3.new(50, 50, 50) }, { AutoUpdate = false }))
		for index = 1, 100 do
			local item = { Position = Vector3.new(if index % 2 == 0 then 0 else 100, 0, index * 0.1) }
			pointZone:Track(item, function()
				return item.Position
			end)
		end
		case("Zone", "Step, 100 tracked points (custom getters)", "Constella.Zone" .. suffix, 2000, function(n)
			for _ = 1, n do
				pointZone:Step()
			end
		end)
		local partZone =
			keep(Zone.new({ CFrame = CFrame.new(), Size = Vector3.new(50, 50, 50) }, { AutoUpdate = false }))
		for index = 1, 100 do
			local part = keep(Instance.new("Part"))
			part.Position = Vector3.new(if index % 2 == 0 then 0 else 100, 0, index * 0.1)
			partZone:Track(part)
		end
		case("Zone", "Step, 100 tracked Parts (built-in getters)", "Constella.Zone" .. suffix, 2000, function(n)
			for _ = 1, n do
				partZone:Step()
			end
		end)

		-- Replication: the remote itself isn't measured (no players here).
		local Replication = Constella.Replication
		for _, delta in { false, true } do
			local replicator = keep(Replication.Server.new(if delta then "BenchDelta" else "BenchFull", {
				Parent = Instance.new("Folder"),
				Delta = delta,
				OnError = noop,
			}))
			if delta and replicator._delta == nil then
				-- This build has no Delta mode; comparing it would measure
				-- full sends under the Delta label.
				replicator:Destroy()
				continue
			end
			replicator._update.FireList = noop
			local share = State.new(inventory(0))
			replicator:Share("Inventory", share)
			local count = 0
			case(
				"Replication",
				"Publish one change to a 40-item inventory",
				(if delta then "Constella.Replication, `Delta = true`" else "Constella.Replication, full value")
					.. suffix,
				2000,
				function(n)
					for _ = 1, n do
						count += 1
						local value = table.clone(share:Get())
						value.Coins = count
						share:Set(value)
					end
				end
			)
		end

		local Data = Constella.Data
		local store = Data.Store.new({
			Name = "Bench",
			Template = { Coins = 0, Inventory = {}, Settings = { Music = true, Volume = 0.5 } },
			Adapter = Data.MemoryAdapter.new(),
			KickOnFailure = false,
			OnError = noop,
		})
		local nextUserId = 0
		case("Data", "Load + release a profile (MemoryAdapter)", "Constella.Data" .. suffix, 300, function(n)
			for _ = 1, n do
				nextUserId += 1
				local fake = { Name = "Bench", UserId = nextUserId, Parent = true, Kick = noop }
				store:LoadAsync(fake):Await()
				store:Release(fake)
			end
		end)

		-- Writing one key of a loaded 20-key profile, four ways. Set and
		-- Update exist in every build; Mutate and CheckWrites are 0.4.0.
		local wideTemplate: { [string]: any } = { Owned = {} }
		for index = 1, 19 do
			wideTemplate["Stat" .. index] = index
		end
		local function loadedProfile(storeName: string, extra: { [string]: any }?): any
			local config: { [string]: any } = {
				Name = storeName,
				Template = wideTemplate,
				Adapter = Data.MemoryAdapter.new(),
				KickOnFailure = false,
				OnError = noop,
			}
			for key, value in (extra or {}) :: { [string]: any } do
				config[key] = value
			end
			local wideStore = Data.Store.new(config :: any)
			nextUserId += 1
			local fake = { Name = "Bench", UserId = nextUserId, Parent = true, Kick = noop }
			local _, loadedOne = wideStore:LoadAsync(fake):Await()
			loadedOne.Changed:Connect(noop)
			return loadedOne
		end
		local wide = loadedProfile("BenchWide")
		local items40 = {}
		for index = 1, 40 do
			items40[index] = { Id = "Item" .. index, Count = index }
		end
		local counter = 0
		case("Data", "Write one key of a 20-key profile", "`profile:Set`" .. suffix, 20000, function(n)
			for _ = 1, n do
				counter += 1
				wide:Set("Stat1", counter)
			end
		end)
		case("Data", "Write one key of a 20-key profile", "`profile:Update`" .. suffix, 20000, function(n)
			for _ = 1, n do
				wide:Update("Stat1", function(value)
					return value + 1
				end)
			end
		end)
		if wide.Mutate then
			case("Data", "Write one key of a 20-key profile", "`profile:Mutate`" .. suffix, 20000, function(n)
				for _ = 1, n do
					wide:Mutate(function(data)
						data.Stat1 += 1
					end)
				end
			end)
			local only = { Keys = { "Stat1" } }
			case(
				"Data",
				"Write one key of a 20-key profile",
				"`profile:Mutate` with `Keys`" .. suffix,
				20000,
				function(n)
					for _ = 1, n do
						wide:Mutate(function(data)
							data.Stat1 += 1
						end, only)
					end
				end
			)
			local checked = loadedProfile("BenchChecked", { CheckWrites = true })
			case(
				"Data",
				"Set a 40-item inventory table",
				"`profile:Set` with `CheckWrites`" .. suffix,
				5000,
				function(n)
					for _ = 1, n do
						checked:Set("Owned", table.clone(items40))
					end
				end
			)
		end
		local unchecked = loadedProfile("BenchPlainTable")
		case("Data", "Set a 40-item inventory table", "`profile:Set`" .. suffix, 5000, function(n)
			for _ = 1, n do
				unchecked:Set("Owned", table.clone(items40))
			end
		end)

		local tag = "ConstellaBench" .. buildIndex
		local tagged = keep(Instance.new("Folder"))
		for _ = 1, 200 do
			local part = Instance.new("Part")
			part.Anchored = true
			CollectionService:AddTag(part, tag)
			part.Parent = tagged
		end
		tagged.Parent = workspace
		case("Component", "Run + Destroy with 200 tagged parts", "Constella.Component" .. suffix, 20, function(n)
			for _ = 1, n do
				local component = Constella.Component.new({ Tag = tag, Start = noop, Stop = noop })
				component:Run()
				component:Destroy()
			end
		end)

		-- A synthetic tick with 50 simulated players (replication sends disabled): coins changing, a request each, a
		-- zone check, a replicated leaderboard update, a broadcast signal
		-- and a few promises.
		local PLAYERS = 50
		local coins, fakes = table.create(PLAYERS), table.create(PLAYERS)
		local tickZone =
			keep(Zone.new({ CFrame = CFrame.new(), Size = Vector3.new(50, 50, 50) }, { AutoUpdate = false }))
		local board = table.create(PLAYERS)
		for index = 1, PLAYERS do
			coins[index] = State.new(0)
			coins[index]:Subscribe(noop)
			fakes[index] = { Name = "Player" .. index }
			local item = { Position = Vector3.new(if index % 2 == 0 then 0 else 100, 0, 0) }
			tickZone:Track(item, function()
				return item.Position
			end)
			board[index] = { Name = "Player" .. index, Score = 0 }
		end
		local tickServer = keep(Network.Server.new("BenchTick", { Parent = Instance.new("Folder"), OnError = noop }))
		local tickBuy = tickServer:Event("Buy", { Schema = schema, RateLimit = { Count = 1e9, Per = 1 } })
		tickBuy:Connect(noop)
		local tickReplicator = keep(Replication.Server.new("BenchTickReplication", {
			Parent = Instance.new("Folder"),
			Delta = true,
			OnError = noop,
		}))
		tickReplicator._update.FireList = noop
		local leaderboard = State.new(board)
		tickReplicator:Share("Leaderboard", leaderboard)
		local tickSignal = Constella.Signal.new()
		for _ = 1, PLAYERS do
			tickSignal:Connect(noop)
		end
		local tick = 0
		case("Scenario", "Synthetic tick, 50 simulated players", "Constella" .. suffix, 200, function(n)
			for _ = 1, n do
				tick += 1
				for index = 1, PLAYERS do
					coins[index]:Set(tick + index)
					tickBuy:_receive(fakes[index], "Sword", 2, { Note = "gift" })
				end
				tickZone:Step()
				local nextBoard = table.clone(leaderboard:Get())
				nextBoard[tick % PLAYERS + 1] = { Name = "Player", Score = tick }
				leaderboard:Set(nextBoard)
				tickSignal:Fire(tick)
				for index = 1, 10 do
					Promise.resolve(index):Then(one)
				end
			end
		end)
	end

	local multiple = #packages > 1
	local builds = {}
	for index, package in packages do
		local suffix = if multiple then (" [%s]"):format(package.Name or package.Module.Name) else ""
		table.insert(builds, { Constella = require(package.Module), suffix = suffix, index = index })
	end
	for _, build in builds do
		currentBuild = build.index
		constellaCases(build.Constella, build.suffix, build.index)
	end
	currentBuild = nil

	if OtherSignal then
		signalCases("sleitnick/signal (errors not isolated)", OtherSignal.new, plain)
		-- Same guarantee as Constella: each listener wrapped in xpcall.
		signalCases("sleitnick/signal + xpcall per listener (errors isolated)", OtherSignal.new, isolated)
	end
	if LemonSignal then
		signalCases("LemonSignal (errors not isolated)", LemonSignal.new, plain)
		signalCases("LemonSignal + xpcall per listener (errors isolated)", LemonSignal.new, isolated)
	end
	if Trove then
		cleanupCases("sleitnick/trove", {
			new = Trove.new,
			addFunction = function(manager, fn)
				manager:Add(fn)
			end,
			addConnection = function(manager, event, fn)
				manager:Connect(event, fn)
			end,
			clean = function(manager)
				manager:Clean()
			end,
		})
	end
	if Janitor then
		cleanupCases("Janitor", {
			new = Janitor.new,
			addFunction = function(manager, fn)
				manager:Add(fn, true)
			end,
			addConnection = function(manager, event, fn)
				manager:Add(event:Connect(fn), "Disconnect")
			end,
			clean = function(manager)
				manager:Cleanup()
			end,
		})
	end
	if OtherPromise then
		promiseCases("evaera/roblox-lua-promise", {
			resolve = OtherPromise.resolve,
			new = OtherPromise.new,
			andThen = function(promise, fn)
				return promise:andThen(fn)
			end,
			await = function(promise)
				return promise:await()
			end,
		})
	end
	case("Pool", "Spawn + despawn a Part", "Clone + Destroy (no pool)", 2000, function(n)
		for _ = 1, n do
			local part = template:Clone()
			part.Parent = folder
			part:Destroy()
		end
	end)
	-- Hand-written baselines without any validation, so the comparison is
	-- about the selection algorithm and not only about validation cost.
	case("Random", "Weighted roll, 100 entries", "Hand-written: sum, then linear scan (each call)", 5000, function(n)
		for _ = 1, n do
			local total = 0
			for _, entry in entries do
				total += entry.Weight
			end
			local roll = rng:NextNumber() * total
			for _, entry in entries do
				roll -= entry.Weight
				if roll < 0 then
					break
				end
			end
		end
	end)
	local cumulative, cumulativeTotal = table.create(#entries), 0
	for index, entry in entries do
		cumulativeTotal += entry.Weight
		cumulative[index] = cumulativeTotal
	end
	case("Random", "Weighted roll, 100 entries", "Hand-written: precomputed totals, linear scan", 50000, function(n)
		for _ = 1, n do
			local roll = rng:NextNumber() * cumulativeTotal
			for index = 1, #cumulative do
				if roll < cumulative[index] then
					break
				end
			end
		end
	end)

	-- Report order: groups and cases in order of first appearance, so every
	-- implementation of a case sits together. Within a case, the builds of
	-- one implementation are next to each other ("X [this build]" then
	-- "X [baseline]"), then the next implementation.
	local firstSeen = {}
	for index, entry in cases do
		firstSeen[entry.group] = firstSeen[entry.group] or index
		local caseKey = entry.group .. "\0" .. entry.name
		firstSeen[caseKey] = firstSeen[caseKey] or index
		local implementationKey = caseKey .. "\0" .. (string.gsub(entry.implementation, " %[[^%]]*%]$", ""))
		firstSeen[implementationKey] = firstSeen[implementationKey] or index
		entry.slot = firstSeen[implementationKey]
		entry.position = entry.slot + index / (#cases + 1)
	end
	table.sort(cases, function(a, b)
		local groupA, groupB = firstSeen[a.group], firstSeen[b.group]
		if groupA ~= groupB then
			return groupA < groupB
		end
		local caseA, caseB = firstSeen[a.group .. "\0" .. a.name], firstSeen[b.group .. "\0" .. b.name]
		if caseA ~= caseB then
			return caseA < caseB
		end
		return a.position < b.position
	end)

	-- The same cases with the builds of each implementation in reverse order.
	-- Every other run uses it, so no build always runs first (straight after
	-- the previous case, whose garbage the collector may still be working on).
	local reversed: { any } = {}
	local first = 1
	while first <= #cases do
		local last = first
		while last < #cases and cases[last + 1].slot == cases[first].slot do
			last += 1
		end
		for index = last, first, -1 do
			table.insert(reversed, cases[index])
		end
		first = last + 1
	end

	for run = 1, runs do
		local order = if run % 2 == 0 then reversed else cases
		for _, entry in order do
			local median = Bench.measure(entry.run, entry.iterations, 5)
			table.insert(entry.samples, median)
		end
	end
	for _, object in fixtures do
		pcall(function()
			object:Destroy()
		end)
	end

	-- Memory ----------------------------------------------------------------
	local COUNT = 5000
	local memory = {}
	local function memoryCase(name, implementation, build, count, trials)
		if not wants(MEMORY_GROUPS[name] or name) then
			return
		end
		local objects = count or COUNT
		table.insert(memory, { name, implementation, Bench.bytesPerObject(build, objects, trials), objects })
	end
	-- Promises allocate several times more per object than a connection, so
	-- 5,000 of them usually overlap a garbage collection step, which makes
	-- the sample smaller. Smaller builds, more of them, avoid that.
	local PROMISE_COUNT, PROMISE_TRIALS = 500, 61
	local function listeners(new)
		return function(count)
			local signal = new()
			for _ = 1, count do
				signal:Connect(noop)
			end
			return signal
		end
	end
	for _, build in builds do
		memoryCase("Connected listener", "Constella.Signal" .. build.suffix, listeners(build.Constella.Signal.new))
	end
	if OtherSignal then
		memoryCase("Connected listener", "sleitnick/signal", listeners(OtherSignal.new))
	end
	if LemonSignal then
		memoryCase("Connected listener", "LemonSignal", listeners(LemonSignal.new))
	end
	-- The functions already exist (`distinct`), so only the manager's own
	-- storage is counted.
	for _, build in builds do
		local Cleanup = build.Constella.Cleanup
		memoryCase("Tracked function", "Constella.Cleanup" .. build.suffix, function(count)
			local manager = Cleanup.new()
			for index = 1, count do
				manager:Add(distinct[index])
			end
			return manager
		end)
	end
	if Trove then
		memoryCase("Tracked function", "sleitnick/trove", function(count)
			local manager = Trove.new()
			for index = 1, count do
				manager:Add(distinct[index])
			end
			return manager
		end)
	end
	if Janitor then
		memoryCase("Tracked function", "Janitor", function(count)
			local manager = Janitor.new()
			for index = 1, count do
				manager:Add(distinct[index], true)
			end
			return manager
		end)
	end
	local function resolvedPromises(resolve)
		return function(count)
			local kept = table.create(count)
			for index = 1, count do
				kept[index] = resolve(index)
			end
			return kept
		end
	end
	for _, build in builds do
		local Promise, suffix = build.Constella.Promise, build.suffix
		-- Each includes the 16-byte array slot that keeps the promise.
		memoryCase(
			"Resolved promise",
			"Constella.Promise" .. suffix,
			resolvedPromises(Promise.resolve),
			PROMISE_COUNT,
			PROMISE_TRIALS
		)
		-- A pending child: the promise, its link to the parent and the
		-- parent's queue entry for it. (Promise.new is not measured: its
		-- executor's work is garbage straight away and would count too.)
		memoryCase("Pending promise from Then", "Constella.Promise" .. suffix, function(count)
			local root = Promise.new(noop)
			local kept = table.create(count)
			for index = 1, count do
				kept[index] = root:Then(one)
			end
			return { root, kept }
		end, PROMISE_COUNT, PROMISE_TRIALS)
	end
	if OtherPromise then
		memoryCase(
			"Resolved promise",
			"evaera/roblox-lua-promise",
			resolvedPromises(OtherPromise.resolve),
			PROMISE_COUNT,
			PROMISE_TRIALS
		)
		memoryCase("Pending promise from Then", "evaera/roblox-lua-promise", function(count)
			local root = OtherPromise.new(noop)
			local kept = table.create(count)
			for index = 1, count do
				kept[index] = root:andThen(one)
			end
			return { root, kept }
		end, PROMISE_COUNT, PROMISE_TRIALS)
	end

	-- Bandwidth: what one update of a 40-item inventory sends. ---------------
	local bandwidth = {}
	local measureLimits = { MaxBytes = math.huge, MaxDepth = 64, MaxNodes = math.huge }
	for _, build in (if wants("Replication") then builds else {}) :: any do
		local Constella, suffix = build.Constella, build.suffix
		for _, delta in { false, true } do
			local replicator = Constella.Replication.Server.new("BenchBandwidth", {
				Parent = Instance.new("Folder"),
				Delta = delta,
				OnError = noop,
			})
			if delta and replicator._delta == nil then
				replicator:Destroy()
				continue
			end
			local sent = {}
			replicator._update.FireList = function(_, _players, ...)
				table.insert(sent, table.pack(...))
			end
			local share = Constella.State.new(inventory(0))
			replicator:Share("Inventory", share)
			local value = table.clone(share:Get())
			value.Coins = 1
			share:Set(value)
			local message = sent[#sent]
			local bytes = Constella.Network.Payload.measure(measureLimits, table.unpack(message, 1, message.n))
			table.insert(bandwidth, {
				(if delta then "Constella.Replication, `Delta = true`" else "Constella.Replication, full value")
					.. suffix,
				bytes,
			})
			replicator:Destroy()
		end
	end

	-- Behaviour checks: guarantees that explain speed differences. -----------
	-- A listener that cancels its runner thread later (for example by adding
	-- coroutine.running() to a cleanup) leaves a dead thread where the
	-- signal expects an idle one. Constella checks for that once per Fire.
	local behaviour = {}
	local function cancelledRunner(label, new)
		local signal = new()
		local runner
		signal:Connect(function()
			runner = coroutine.running()
		end)
		signal:Fire()
		task.cancel(runner)
		local calls = 0
		signal:Connect(function()
			calls += 1
		end)
		local ok = pcall(signal.Fire, signal)
		table.insert(
			behaviour,
			{ label, if ok and calls == 1 then "keeps working" else "Fire raises an error, listeners don't run" }
		)
	end
	if wants("Signal") then
		for _, build in builds do
			cancelledRunner("Constella.Signal" .. build.suffix, build.Constella.Signal.new)
		end
		if OtherSignal then
			cancelledRunner("sleitnick/signal", OtherSignal.new)
		end
		if LemonSignal then
			cancelledRunner("LemonSignal", LemonSignal.new)
		end
	end

	-- Leak checks: the owner stays alive; released objects must be freed. ------
	local LEAK_COUNT = 2000
	local leaks = {}
	local owners = {}
	local function leakCase(name, build)
		-- Leak names start with their group ("Signal: ...").
		if not wants((string.match(name, "^(%a+):") or name) :: string) then
			return
		end
		local remaining, seconds = Bench.leakCheck(build, 15)
		table.insert(leaks, { name, LEAK_COUNT, remaining, seconds })
	end
	for _, build in builds do
		local Constella, suffix = build.Constella, build.suffix
		leakCase("Signal: disconnected listeners (signal kept alive)" .. suffix, function()
			local signal = Constella.Signal.new()
			owners.signal = signal
			local objects, connections = {}, {}
			for index = 1, LEAK_COUNT do
				local listener = function()
					return index
				end
				table.insert(objects, listener)
				table.insert(connections, signal:Connect(listener))
			end
			signal:Fire()
			return objects,
				function()
					for _, connection in connections do
						connection:Disconnect()
					end
				end
		end)
		leakCase("Signal: listeners of kept, disconnected connections" .. suffix, function()
			local signal = Constella.Signal.new()
			owners.signal = signal
			local objects, connections = {}, {}
			for index = 1, LEAK_COUNT do
				local listener = function()
					return index
				end
				table.insert(objects, listener)
				table.insert(connections, signal:Connect(listener))
			end
			signal:Fire()
			owners.connections = connections -- the connections themselves stay referenced
			return objects,
				function()
					for _, connection in connections do
						connection:Disconnect()
					end
				end
		end)
		leakCase("Cleanup: cleaned resources (manager kept alive)" .. suffix, function()
			local manager = Constella.Cleanup.new()
			owners.cleanup = manager
			local objects = {}
			for index = 1, LEAK_COUNT do
				local resource = function()
					return index
				end
				table.insert(objects, resource)
				manager:Add(resource)
			end
			return objects, function()
				manager:Clean()
			end
		end)
		leakCase("State: unsubscribed callbacks (state kept alive)" .. suffix, function()
			local value = Constella.State.new(0)
			owners.state = value
			local objects, connections = {}, {}
			for index = 1, LEAK_COUNT do
				local callback = function()
					return index
				end
				table.insert(objects, callback)
				table.insert(connections, value:Subscribe(callback))
			end
			value:Set(1)
			return objects,
				function()
					for _, connection in connections do
						connection:Disconnect()
					end
				end
		end)
		leakCase("Pool: objects destroyed past MaxIdle (pool kept alive)" .. suffix, function()
			local pool = Constella.Pool.new({
				Create = function()
					return {}
				end,
				MaxIdle = 0,
			})
			owners.pool = pool
			local objects = {}
			for _ = 1, LEAK_COUNT do
				table.insert(objects, pool:Acquire())
			end
			return objects, function()
				for _, object in objects do
					pool:Release(object)
				end
			end
		end)
		leakCase("Promise: values of promises a kept chain came from" .. suffix, function()
			local Promise = Constella.Promise
			local objects, chains = {}, {}
			for _ = 1, LEAK_COUNT do
				local payload = {}
				table.insert(objects, payload)
				table.insert(chains, Promise.resolve(payload):Then(one))
			end
			owners.chains = chains -- the end of each chain stays referenced
			-- One more job, so a recycled handler thread doesn't hold the
			-- last payload in an unused stack slot (bounded, not a leak).
			Promise.resolve(nil):Then(one)
			return objects, function() end
		end)
		table.clear(owners)
	end

	-- Report ------------------------------------------------------------------------
	-- version() is deprecated, but its replacement RunService:GetRobloxVersion()
	-- needs RobloxScript capability, which the command bar and plugins lack.
	-- selene: allow(undefined_variable)
	local hasVersion, engineVersion = pcall(version)
	local lines = {
		("Runs: %d (each the median of 5 trials). Roblox %s."):format(
			runs,
			if hasVersion then tostring(engineVersion) else "(version unavailable)"
		),
		"",
	}

	-- A/B: the first build against the second, case by case.
	local comparisons = {}
	local regressions = {}
	if multiple then
		local byKey = {}
		for _, entry in cases do
			if entry.build then
				byKey[entry.slot .. ":" .. entry.build] = entry
			end
		end
		local intervalRng = Random.new(20261114)
		for _, entry in cases do
			local baseline = entry.build == 1 and byKey[entry.slot .. ":2"]
			if baseline then
				local ratio, lower, upper = Bench.ratioInterval(entry.samples, baseline.samples, intervalRng)
				local label = if upper < 0.97 then "faster" elseif lower > 1.03 then "slower" else "same"
				comparisons[entry] = ("%+.0f%% [%+.0f, %+.0f] %s"):format(
					(ratio - 1) * 100,
					(lower - 1) * 100,
					(upper - 1) * 100,
					label
				)
				if ratio > REGRESSION_RATIO and lower > REGRESSION_LOWER then
					table.insert(
						regressions,
						("REGRESSION | %s: %s | %s | %s"):format(
							entry.group,
							entry.name,
							entry.implementation,
							comparisons[entry]
						)
					)
				end
			end
		end
	end

	table.insert(
		lines,
		"| Group | Case | Implementation | Median µs/op | Best run | Worst run | vs baseline (95% CI) |"
	)
	table.insert(lines, "| --- | --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |")
	for _, entry in cases do
		entry.inRunOrder = table.clone(entry.samples)
		table.sort(entry.samples)
		local count = #entry.samples
		table.insert(
			lines,
			("| %s | %s | %s | %.3f | %.3f | %.3f | %s |"):format(
				entry.group,
				entry.name,
				entry.implementation,
				Bench.median(entry.samples),
				entry.samples[1],
				entry.samples[count],
				comparisons[entry] or ""
			)
		)
	end
	table.insert(lines, "")
	if #regressions > 0 then
		table.insert(lines, "Regressions (more than 10% slower, 95% interval above +5%):")
		table.insert(lines, "")
		for _, line in regressions do
			table.insert(lines, line)
		end
	else
		table.insert(lines, "No regressions.")
	end

	-- Every run's result, in the order the runs happened.
	table.insert(lines, "")
	local header, divider = { "| Case | Implementation |" }, { "| --- | --- |" }
	for run = 1, runs do
		table.insert(header, (" Run %d |"):format(run))
		table.insert(divider, " ---: |")
	end
	table.insert(lines, table.concat(header))
	table.insert(lines, table.concat(divider))
	for _, entry in cases do
		local cells = { ("| %s: %s | %s |"):format(entry.group, entry.name, entry.implementation) }
		for _, sample in entry.inRunOrder do
			table.insert(cells, (" %.3f |"):format(sample))
		end
		table.insert(lines, table.concat(cells))
	end

	table.insert(lines, "")
	table.insert(lines, "| Memory per object | Implementation | Bytes | Objects per build |")
	table.insert(lines, "| --- | --- | ---: | ---: |")
	for _, row in memory do
		table.insert(lines, ("| %s | %s | %d | %d |"):format(row[1], row[2], math.floor(row[3] + 0.5), row[4]))
	end
	table.insert(lines, "")
	table.insert(lines, "| Estimated payload per update (one field of a 40-item inventory changes) | Estimated bytes |")
	table.insert(lines, "| --- | ---: |")
	for _, row in bandwidth do
		table.insert(lines, ("| %s | %d |"):format(row[1], row[2]))
	end
	if #behaviour > 0 then
		table.insert(lines, "")
		table.insert(lines, "| Signal: after user code cancels an idle runner thread | Result |")
		table.insert(lines, "| --- | --- |")
		for _, row in behaviour do
			table.insert(lines, ("| %s | %s |"):format(row[1], row[2]))
		end
	end
	table.insert(lines, "")
	table.insert(lines, "| Leak check | Released | Still alive | Seconds |")
	table.insert(lines, "| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |")
	for _, row in leaks do
		table.insert(lines, ("| %s | %d | %d | %.1f |"):format(row[1], row[2], row[3], row[4]))
	end
	return table.concat(lines, "\n")
end

-- Sounds load once they're in the DataModel, report their TimeLength, and
-- a sound that never loads stays "playing" without time passing.
local function sound(id, parent)
    local s = Instance.new("Sound")
    s.SoundId = id
    s.Parent = parent
    return s
end

local ogg = sound("rbxasset://sounds/oof.ogg", workspace)
local mp3 = sound("rbxasset://sounds/action_jump.mp3", workspace)
local loose = sound("rbxasset://sounds/oof.ogg", nil)
local missing = sound("rbxasset://sounds/no_such_sound.wav", workspace)
log("before loading", ogg.IsLoaded, ogg.TimeLength)

for _ = 1, 100 do
    if ogg.IsLoaded and mp3.IsLoaded then
        break
    end
    task.wait(0.05)
end
log("ogg", ogg.IsLoaded, string.format("%.6f", ogg.TimeLength))
log("mp3", mp3.IsLoaded, string.format("%.6f", mp3.TimeLength))
log("unparented", loose.IsLoaded, loose.TimeLength)

missing:Play()
mp3:Play()
task.wait(0.15)
log("missing", missing.IsLoaded, missing.Playing, missing.TimePosition)
log("mp3 playing", mp3.Playing, mp3.TimePosition > 0.05)
task.wait(0.5)
-- Past its end (0.34 s): stopped and rewound.
log("mp3 ended", mp3.Playing, mp3.TimePosition)

for _, s in { ogg, mp3, loose, missing } do
    s:Destroy()
end

-- IMPLIED, INCLUDING BUT NOT LIMITED TO THE WARRANTIES OF MERCHANTABILITY,
-- FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE AND NONINFRINGEMENT. IN NO EVENT SHALL THE
-- AUTHORS OR COPYRIGHT HOLDERS BE LIABLE FOR ANY CLAIM, DAMAGES OR OTHER
-- LIABILITY, WHETHER IN AN ACTION OF CONTRACT, TORT OR OTHERWISE, ARISING FROM,
-- OUT OF OR IN CONNECTION WITH THE SOFTWARE OR THE USE OR OTHER DEALINGS IN THE
-- SOFTWARE.

--!strict
local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage")
local Cleanup = require(ReplicatedStorage:WaitForChild("Packages"):WaitForChild("Constella"):WaitForChild("Cleanup"))

local cleanup = Cleanup.new()

-- Instances, connections, threads and functions are detected automatically.
local part = cleanup:Add(Instance.new("Part"))
part.Anchored = true
part.Position = Vector3.new(0, 10, 0)
part.Parent = workspace

cleanup:Connect(part.Touched, function(hit: BasePart)
	print("[Cleanup] touched by", hit.Name)
end)

cleanup:Add(task.spawn(function()
	while true do
		part.CFrame *= CFrame.Angles(0, math.rad(5), 0)
		task.wait()
	end
end))

-- Keyed resources replace (and clean) whatever was there before.
local highlight = Instance.new("Highlight")
highlight.Parent = part
cleanup:Set("highlight", highlight)
local selectionBox = Instance.new("SelectionBox")
selectionBox.Adornee = part
selectionBox.Parent = part
cleanup:Set("highlight", selectionBox) -- the Highlight is destroyed

cleanup:Add(function()
	print("[Cleanup] all resources released")
end)

task.wait(3)
cleanup:Destroy() -- stops the loop, disconnects, destroys the part
