--!strict
--!native
--!optimize 2

const Actor = script:GetActor()

const Tracks: { [Animator]: { [Animation]: AnimationTrack } } = {}

-- Speed of every track currently held at zero by a Time Stop. A track already
-- in the map is skipped by a later hold — the first one owns the restore.
const HeldSpeeds: { [AnimationTrack]: number } = {}

-- Hold every playing clip of `models` at speed zero, remembering each
-- track's speed. Tracks already held (Speed == 0) are skipped.
const function pauseModels(models: { Model })
	for _, character in models do
		if typeof(character) ~= "Instance" then continue end
		if not character:IsA("Model") then continue end

		const animator = character:FindFirstChildWhichIsA("Animator", true)
		if not animator then continue end

		for _, track in animator:GetPlayingAnimationTracks() do
			if HeldSpeeds[track] ~= nil then continue end
			if track.Speed == 0 then continue end
			HeldSpeeds[track] = track.Speed
			track:AdjustSpeed(0)
		end
	end
end

-- Hand the remembered speeds back to the still-alive tracks and forget the
-- rest.
const function resumeModels(models: { Model })
	for _, character in models do
		if typeof(character) ~= "Instance" then continue end
		if not character:IsA("Model") then continue end

		const animator = character:FindFirstChildWhichIsA("Animator", true)
		if not animator then continue end

		for _, track in animator:GetPlayingAnimationTracks() do
			const speed = HeldSpeeds[track]
			if speed == nil then continue end

			HeldSpeeds[track] = nil
			track:AdjustSpeed(speed)
		end
	end
end

Actor:BindToMessage("PauseAll", function(models: { Model }?)
	if type(models) ~= "table" then return end
	pauseModels(models)
end)

Actor:BindToMessage("ResumeAll", function(models: { Model }?)
	if type(models) ~= "table" then return end
	resumeModels(models)
end)

type AnimationsPlayProps = {
	Priority: Enum.AnimationPriority?,
	Speed: number?,
	FadeInTime: number?,
	Weight: number?,
	-- Looping is a property of the AnimationTrack, not of the Animation asset.
	Looped: boolean?,
}
Actor:BindToMessage(
	"Play",
	function(character: Model, animation: Animation, props: AnimationsPlayProps?)
		const animator = character:FindFirstChildWhichIsA("Animator", true)
		if not animator then return end

		props = props
			or {
				Priority = Enum.AnimationPriority.Action,
				Speed = 1,
				FadeInTime = 0,
				Weight = 1,
			}

		if not Tracks[animator] then
			Tracks[animator] = {}

			animator.Destroying:Once(function()
				Tracks[animator] = nil
			end)
		end

		const track = Tracks[animator][animation] or animator:LoadAnimation(animation)
		Tracks[animator][animation] = track
		track.Looped = props.Looped == true
		track:Play(props.FadeInTime, props.Weight, props.Speed)
	end
)

type AnimationsStopProps = {
	FadeOutTime: number?,
}
Actor:BindToMessage(
	"Stop",
	function(character: Model, animation: Animation, props: AnimationsStopProps?)
		const animator = character:FindFirstChildWhichIsA("Animator", true)
		if not animator then return end

		if not Tracks[animator] or not Tracks[animator][animation] then return end

		props = props or {
			FadeOutTime = 0,
		}

		Tracks[animator][animation]:Stop(props.FadeOutTime)
	end
)

--!strict
--[=[
	Constella.Component

	Attaches behaviour to every Instance with a CollectionService tag.

	```lua
	local Spinner = { Tag = "Spinner" }

	function Spinner:Start()
		self.Cleanup:Connect(RunService.Heartbeat, function(dt)
			self.Instance.CFrame *= CFrame.Angles(0, dt, 0)
		end)
	end

	local spinners = Component.new(Spinner)
	spinners:Run()
	```

	Semantics
	- An object is created for a tagged instance only while the instance is
	  inside one of `Ancestors` (default: { workspace }) and passes `Filter`.
	  Moving it out (or streaming it out on a client) detaches it; moving it
	  back attaches a fresh object.
	- Each object has `self.Instance`, `self.Cleanup` (destroyed on detach)
	  and `self.Component` (the manager). Methods are looked up on the
	  definition table, so `function Spinner:Foo()` is available as `self:Foo()`.
	- Start runs on its own thread. If it errors before yielding, the object
	  is detached and the error reported; Added does not fire.
	- On detach: Stop runs, then the object's Cleanup is destroyed, then
	  Removed fires. Errors are reported, never swallowed.
]=]

local CollectionService = game:GetService("CollectionService")

local Signal = require(script.Parent.Signal)
local Cleanup = require(script.Parent.Cleanup)

export type Definition = {
	Tag: string,
	Ancestors: { Instance }?,
	Filter: ((instance: Instance) -> boolean)?,
	Start: ((self: Definition) -> ())?,
	Stop: ((self: Definition) -> ())?,
	[string]: any,
}

export type Options = {
	OnError: ((message: string) -> ())?,
}

export type Object = {
	Instance: Instance,
	Cleanup: Cleanup.Cleanup,
	Component: any,
	[string]: any,
}

export type Component = {
	Tag: string,
	Added: Signal.Signal<any>,
	Removed: Signal.Signal<any>,
	Run: (self: Component) -> (),
	Get: (self: Component, instance: Instance) -> any,
	GetAll: (self: Component) -> { any },
	Destroy: (self: Component) -> (),
}

local PREFIX = "[Constella.Component] "

local function traceback(err: any): string
	return debug.traceback(tostring(err), 2)
end

local ComponentClass = {}
ComponentClass.__index = ComponentClass

local function qualifies(self: any, instance: Instance): boolean
	if not CollectionService:HasTag(instance, self.Tag) then
		return false
	end
	local inside = false
	for _, ancestor in self._ancestors do
		if instance:IsDescendantOf(ancestor) then
			inside = true
			break
		end
	end
	if not inside then
		return false
	end
	local filter = self._definition.Filter
	if filter then
		local ok, result = pcall(filter, instance)
		if not ok then
			self._onError(PREFIX .. ("Filter for '%s' failed: %s"):format(self.Tag, tostring(result)))
			return false
		end
		return result == true
	end
	return true
end

local function detach(self: any, instance: Instance)
	local object = self._objects[instance]
	if object == nil then
		return
	end
	self._objects[instance] = nil
	local startup = object._startup
	object._startup = nil
	if startup and startup ~= coroutine.running() and coroutine.status(startup) ~= "dead" then
		task.cancel(startup)
	end
	local definition = self._definition
	if definition.Stop and object._started then
		local ok, err = xpcall(definition.Stop, traceback, object)
		if not ok then
			self._onError(PREFIX .. ("Stop failed for %s: %s"):format(instance:GetFullName(), tostring(err)))
		end
	end
	local ok, err = pcall(function()
		object.Cleanup:Destroy()
	end)
	if not ok then
		self._onError(PREFIX .. ("Cleanup failed for %s: %s"):format(instance:GetFullName(), tostring(err)))
	end
	if object._announced then
		self.Removed:Fire(object)
	end
end

local function attach(self: any, instance: Instance)
	if self._objects[instance] then
		return
	end
	local object: any = setmetatable({
		Instance = instance,
		Cleanup = Cleanup.new(),
		Component = self,
		_started = false,
		_announced = false,
	}, self._objectMeta)
	self._objects[instance] = object

	local definition = self._definition
	if definition.Start then
		local synchronous = true
		local failed = false
		object._started = true
		local startup = coroutine.create(function()
			local ok, err = xpcall(definition.Start, traceback, object)
			object._startup = nil
			if not ok then
				self._onError(PREFIX .. ("Start failed for %s: %s"):format(instance:GetFullName(), tostring(err)))
				if synchronous then
					failed = true
				end
			end
		end)
		object._startup = startup
		task.spawn(startup)
		synchronous = false
		if failed then
			object._started = false -- Stop is for objects whose Start succeeded or is running
			detach(self, instance)
			return
		end
	end
	-- Start may have detached the object (e.g. by removing the tag).
	if self._objects[instance] == object then
		object._announced = true
		self.Added:Fire(object)
	end
end

local function evaluate(self: any, instance: Instance)
	if self._destroyed then
		return
	end
	if qualifies(self, instance) then
		attach(self, instance)
	else
		detach(self, instance)
	end
end

local function watch(self: any, instance: Instance)
	if self._watched[instance] then
		return
	end
	self._watched[instance] = instance.AncestryChanged:Connect(function()
		evaluate(self, instance)
	end)
	evaluate(self, instance)
end

local function unwatch(self: any, instance: Instance)
	local connection = self._watched[instance]
	if connection then
		connection:Disconnect()
		self._watched[instance] = nil
	end
	detach(self, instance)
end

--- Starts observing the tag. Connect to Added/Removed first if you need
--- events for instances that already exist.
function ComponentClass.Run(self: any)
	if self._destroyed then
		error(PREFIX .. "Cannot run a destroyed Component", 2)
	end
	if self._running then
		error(PREFIX .. ("Component '%s' is already running"):format(self.Tag), 2)
	end
	self._running = true
	self._cleanup:Connect(CollectionService:GetInstanceAddedSignal(self.Tag), function(instance: Instance)
		watch(self, instance)
	end)
	self._cleanup:Connect(CollectionService:GetInstanceRemovedSignal(self.Tag), function(instance: Instance)
		unwatch(self, instance)
	end)
	for _, instance in CollectionService:GetTagged(self.Tag) do
		watch(self, instance)
	end
end

--- Returns the object attached to `instance`, or nil.
function ComponentClass.Get(self: any, instance: Instance): any
	return self._objects[instance]
end

function ComponentClass.GetAll(self: any): { any }
	local objects = {}
	for _, object in self._objects do
		table.insert(objects, object)
	end
	return objects
end

--- Detaches every object (Stop, Cleanup, Removed) and stops observing.
function ComponentClass.Destroy(self: any)
	if self._destroyed then
		return
	end
	self._destroyed = true
	self._cleanup:Destroy()
	local instances = {}
	for instance in self._watched do
		table.insert(instances, instance)
	end
	for _, instance in instances do
		unwatch(self, instance)
	end
	self.Added:Destroy()
	self.Removed:Destroy()
end

local Component = {}

function Component.new(definition: Definition, options: Options?): Component
	if type(definition) ~= "table" then
		error(PREFIX .. "Component.new expects a definition table", 2)
	end
	if type(definition.Tag) ~= "string" or definition.Tag == "" then
		error(PREFIX .. "Definition needs a non-empty string Tag", 2)
	end
	for _, field in { "Start", "Stop", "Filter" } do
		local value = definition[field]
		if value ~= nil and type(value) ~= "function" then
			error(PREFIX .. ("Definition %s must be a function"):format(field), 2)
		end
	end
	local ancestors: { any } = definition.Ancestors or { workspace }
	if type(ancestors) ~= "table" or #ancestors == 0 then
		error(PREFIX .. "Ancestors must be a non-empty array of Instances", 2)
	end
	for _, ancestor in ancestors do
		if typeof(ancestor) ~= "Instance" then
			error(PREFIX .. "Ancestors must be a non-empty array of Instances", 2)
		end
	end
	if options ~= nil and options.OnError ~= nil and type(options.OnError) ~= "function" then
		error(PREFIX .. "OnError must be a function", 2)
	end

	local self = setmetatable({
		Tag = definition.Tag,
		Added = Signal.new(),
		Removed = Signal.new(),
		_definition = definition,
		_objectMeta = { __index = definition },
		_ancestors = table.clone(ancestors),
		_objects = {},
		_watched = {},
		_cleanup = Cleanup.new(),
		_running = false,
		_destroyed = false,
		_onError = (options and options.OnError) or function(message: string)
			task.spawn(error, message, 0)
		end,
	}, ComponentClass)
	return (self :: any) :: Component
end

return table.freeze(Component)

--!strict
--[=[
	Constella.Core

	Explicit application instances that own services (server) or
	controllers (client) and run their lifecycle in dependency order.

	```lua
	local app = Constella.App.new()
	app:Add(require(script.Services.InventoryService))
	app:Start()
	```

	Lifecycle
	1. Add       - definitions are validated (name, duplicates, environment).
	2. Start     - dependencies are resolved: missing dependencies and cycles
	               fail before any user code runs.
	             - Init runs for every definition, sequentially, in
	               dependency order. Init may yield.
	             - Start runs for every definition in dependency order, each
	               on its own thread. An error raised before Start first
	               yields fails startup; an error after a yield is reported
	               through OnError and the app keeps running.
	             - A definition with WaitForStart = true is a readiness
	               gate: Start (yields included) must finish before later
	               definitions start and before the app is Running. An
	               error at any point, or running past StartTimeout
	               (default 30s), fails startup. App:Start then yields.
	             - If startup fails, Stop runs (reverse order) for every
	               definition whose Init completed, their Cleanup is
	               destroyed and Start raises the error. The app is then
	               "Failed" and cannot be restarted.
	3. Stop      - Stop runs in reverse dependency order, then each
	               context's Cleanup is destroyed. Idempotent.

	A Start that is still running when its definition stops (it yielded and
	never returned, like a `while true do ... task.wait() end` loop) is
	cancelled just before that definition's Stop, both on App:Stop and on
	a failed startup. Threads that Start spawns itself are not tracked: add
	them to context.Cleanup.

	An app can only be started once.
]=]

local Signal = require(script.Parent.Signal)
local Cleanup = require(script.Parent.Cleanup)

export type Environment = "Server" | "Client" | "Shared"
export type AppState = "Idle" | "Starting" | "Running" | "Stopping" | "Stopped" | "Failed"

export type Context = {
	--- The app this definition belongs to.
	App: App,
	--- The definition's name.
	Name: string,
	--- Destroyed automatically after Stop (or after a failed startup).
	Cleanup: Cleanup.Cleanup,
	--- Returns a declared dependency. Undeclared names raise an error.
	Get: (self: Context, name: string) -> any,
}

export type Definition = {
	Name: string,
	Dependencies: { string }?,
	Environment: Environment?,
	Init: ((self: Definition, context: Context) -> ())?,
	Start: ((self: Definition, context: Context) -> ())?,
	Stop: ((self: Definition, context: Context) -> ())?,
	--- Make App:Start wait for this definition's Start to finish (even if it
	--- yields). Any Start error then fails startup. Defaults to false.
	WaitForStart: boolean?,
	--- Seconds a WaitForStart definition may take. Defaults to 30.
	StartTimeout: number?,
	[string]: any,
}

export type AppOptions = {
	Name: string?,
	--- Defaults to "Server" on the server and "Client" on a client.
	Environment: ("Server" | "Client")?,
	--- Receives errors that cannot be raised to a caller (errors thrown by
	--- Start after it yielded). Defaults to re-raising on a new thread.
	OnError: ((message: string) -> ())?,
}

export type AddModulesOptions = {
	Recursive: boolean?,
	Filter: ((module: ModuleScript) -> boolean)?,
}

export type App = {
	Name: string,
	Environment: "Server" | "Client",
	Started: Signal.Signal<()>,
	Stopped: Signal.Signal<()>,
	Add: <T>(self: App, definition: T) -> T,
	AddModules: (self: App, container: Instance, options: AddModulesOptions?) -> { any },
	Get: (self: App, name: string) -> any,
	Has: (self: App, name: string) -> boolean,
	GetOrder: (self: App) -> { string },
	GetState: (self: App) -> AppState,
	Start: (self: App) -> (),
	AwaitStart: (self: App) -> (),
	Stop: (self: App) -> (),
}

local PREFIX = "[Constella.App] "
local LIFECYCLE_METHODS = { "Init", "Start", "Stop" }
local DEFAULT_START_TIMEOUT = 30

local function traceback(err: any): string
	return debug.traceback(tostring(err), 2)
end

local function detectEnvironment(): "Server" | "Client"
	local RunService = game:GetService("RunService")
	if RunService:IsServer() then
		return "Server"
	end
	return "Client"
end

local function validateDefinition(app: any, definition: any, source: string?, level: number)
	local where = if source then (" (from %s)"):format(source) else ""
	if type(definition) ~= "table" then
		error(PREFIX .. ("Definition must be a table, got %s%s"):format(typeof(definition), where), level)
	end
	local name = definition.Name
	if type(name) ~= "string" or name == "" then
		error(PREFIX .. ("Definition needs a non-empty string Name%s"):format(where), level)
	end
	if app._byName[name] ~= nil then
		error(PREFIX .. ("'%s' was already added to app '%s'%s"):format(name, app.Name, where), level)
	end

	local dependencies = definition.Dependencies
	if dependencies ~= nil then
		if type(dependencies) ~= "table" then
			error(PREFIX .. ("'%s'.Dependencies must be an array of names"):format(name), level)
		end
		local seen = {}
		for index, dependency in dependencies do
			if type(index) ~= "number" or type(dependency) ~= "string" then
				error(PREFIX .. ("'%s'.Dependencies must be an array of names"):format(name), level)
			end
			if dependency == name then
				error(PREFIX .. ("'%s' cannot depend on itself"):format(name), level)
			end
			if seen[dependency] then
				error(PREFIX .. ("'%s' lists dependency '%s' twice"):format(name, dependency), level)
			end
			seen[dependency] = true
		end
	end

	for _, method in LIFECYCLE_METHODS do
		local value = definition[method]
		if value ~= nil and type(value) ~= "function" then
			error(PREFIX .. ("'%s'.%s must be a function, got %s"):format(name, method, typeof(value)), level)
		end
	end

	if definition.WaitForStart ~= nil and type(definition.WaitForStart) ~= "boolean" then
		error(PREFIX .. ("'%s'.WaitForStart must be a boolean"):format(name), level)
	end
	local startTimeout = definition.StartTimeout
	if
		startTimeout ~= nil
		and (type(startTimeout) ~= "number" or not (startTimeout > 0) or startTimeout == math.huge)
	then
		error(PREFIX .. ("'%s'.StartTimeout must be a positive number of seconds"):format(name), level)
	end

	local environment = definition.Environment
	if environment ~= nil and environment ~= "Server" and environment ~= "Client" and environment ~= "Shared" then
		error(PREFIX .. ('\'%s\'.Environment must be "Server", "Client" or "Shared"'):format(name), level)
	end
	if environment ~= nil and environment ~= "Shared" and environment ~= app.Environment then
		error(
			PREFIX
				.. ("'%s' is a %s-only definition and cannot be added to a %s app"):format(
					name,
					environment:lower(),
					app.Environment:lower()
				),
			level
		)
	end
end

local function resolveOrder(app: any): { any }
	-- Report every missing dependency at once.
	local missing = {}
	for _, definition in app._definitions do
		for _, dependency in definition.Dependencies or {} do
			if app._byName[dependency] == nil then
				table.insert(missing, ("'%s' -> '%s'"):format(definition.Name, dependency))
			end
		end
	end
	if #missing > 0 then
		error(PREFIX .. "Missing dependencies (not added to the app): " .. table.concat(missing, ", "), 0)
	end

	-- Depth-first topological sort. Deterministic: definitions are visited in
	-- registration order, dependencies in declared order.
	local order = {}
	local marks: { [string]: "visiting" | "done" } = {}
	local path: { string } = {}

	local function visit(definition: any)
		local name = definition.Name
		local mark = marks[name]
		if mark == "done" then
			return
		end
		if mark == "visiting" then
			local start = table.find(path, name) :: number
			local cycle = table.move(path, start, #path, 1, {})
			table.insert(cycle, name)
			error(PREFIX .. "Circular dependency: " .. table.concat(cycle, " -> "), 0)
		end
		marks[name] = "visiting"
		table.insert(path, name)
		for _, dependency in definition.Dependencies or {} do
			visit(app._byName[dependency])
		end
		table.remove(path)
		marks[name] = "done"
		table.insert(order, definition)
	end

	for _, definition in app._definitions do
		visit(definition)
	end
	return order
end

local function createContext(app: any, definition: any): Context
	local allowed = {}
	for _, dependency in definition.Dependencies or {} do
		allowed[dependency] = true
	end
	local context = {
		App = app,
		Name = definition.Name,
		Cleanup = Cleanup.new(),
	}
	function context.Get(_: any, name: string): any
		if not allowed[name] then
			error(
				PREFIX
					.. ("'%s' accessed '%s' without listing it in Dependencies"):format(definition.Name, tostring(name)),
				2
			)
		end
		return app._byName[name]
	end
	return table.freeze(context) :: any
end

-- Runs Stop (reverse order) and destroys each context's Cleanup.
-- Returns the collected error messages; never throws.
local function teardown(app: any, definitions: { any }): { string }
	local errors = {}
	for index = #definitions, 1, -1 do
		local definition = definitions[index]
		local context = app._contexts[definition.Name]
		-- A Start that is still running (it yielded and never returned) must
		-- not keep working while its definition stops.
		local startThread = app._startThreads[definition.Name]
		if startThread then
			app._startThreads[definition.Name] = nil
			if coroutine.status(startThread) == "suspended" then
				pcall(task.cancel, startThread)
			end
		end
		if definition.Stop then
			local ok, err = xpcall(definition.Stop, traceback, definition, context)
			if not ok then
				table.insert(errors, ("Stop failed for '%s': %s"):format(definition.Name, err))
			end
		end
		local ok, err = pcall(function()
			context.Cleanup:Destroy()
		end)
		if not ok then
			table.insert(errors, ("Cleanup failed for '%s': %s"):format(definition.Name, tostring(err)))
		end
	end
	return errors
end

-- Resumes a waiting thread unless it was cancelled while it waited (then it
-- is dead, and resuming it would raise).
local function resume(thread: thread, ...: any)
	if coroutine.status(thread) == "suspended" then
		task.spawn(thread, ...)
	end
end

local function resumeWaiters(app: any, ok: boolean, message: string?)
	local waiting = app._waiting
	app._waiting = {}
	for _, thread in waiting do
		resume(thread, ok, message)
	end
end

local AppClass = {}
AppClass.__index = AppClass

local function add(self: any, definition: any, source: string?, level: number): any
	if self._state ~= "Idle" then
		local name = if type(definition) == "table" then tostring(definition.Name) else "?"
		error(PREFIX .. ("Cannot add '%s': app '%s' has already been started"):format(name, self.Name), level)
	end
	validateDefinition(self, definition, source, level + 1)
	self._byName[definition.Name] = definition
	table.insert(self._definitions, definition)
	return definition
end

--- Registers a service/controller definition. Returns it unchanged.
function AppClass.Add(self: any, definition: any): any
	return add(self, definition, nil, 3)
end

--- Requires and adds every ModuleScript in `container` (children only,
--- or all descendants with `Recursive = true`), sorted by full name so the
--- result does not depend on instance order. This is explicit: nothing is
--- discovered unless you point it at a container.
function AppClass.AddModules(self: any, container: Instance, options: AddModulesOptions?): { any }
	if typeof(container) ~= "Instance" then
		error(PREFIX .. ("AddModules expects an Instance, got %s"):format(typeof(container)), 2)
	end
	local recursive = options ~= nil and options.Recursive == true
	local filter = if options then options.Filter else nil
	local candidates: { Instance } = if recursive then container:GetDescendants() else container:GetChildren()
	local modules = {}
	for _, instance in candidates do
		if instance:IsA("ModuleScript") and (filter == nil or filter(instance)) then
			table.insert(modules, instance)
		end
	end
	table.sort(modules, function(a, b)
		return a:GetFullName() < b:GetFullName()
	end)

	local added = {}
	for _, module in modules do
		local ok, result = pcall(require, module)
		if not ok then
			error(PREFIX .. ("Failed to require %s: %s"):format(module:GetFullName(), tostring(result)), 2)
		end
		table.insert(added, add(self, result, module:GetFullName(), 3))
	end
	return added
end

--- Returns the definition registered under `name`.
function AppClass.Get(self: any, name: string): any
	local definition = self._byName[name]
	if definition == nil then
		error(PREFIX .. ("'%s' was not added to app '%s'"):format(tostring(name), self.Name), 2)
	end
	return definition
end

function AppClass.Has(self: any, name: string): boolean
	return self._byName[name] ~= nil
end

--- Returns the resolved startup order (empty until Start).
function AppClass.GetOrder(self: any): { string }
	local names = {}
	for _, definition in self._order do
		table.insert(names, definition.Name)
	end
	return names
end

function AppClass.GetState(self: any): AppState
	return self._state
end

local function fail(self: any, message: string)
	self._state = "Failed"
	self._failure = message
	resumeWaiters(self, false, message)
	error(message, 0)
end

function AppClass.Start(self: any)
	if self._state ~= "Idle" then
		error(
			PREFIX
				.. ("Cannot start app '%s': it is %s (an app can only be started once)"):format(
					self.Name,
					self._state:lower()
				),
			2
		)
	end
	self._state = "Starting"

	local resolved, orderOrError = pcall(resolveOrder, self)
	if not resolved then
		fail(self, tostring(orderOrError))
	end
	local order = orderOrError :: { any }
	self._order = order

	-- Init: sequential, in dependency order. Fail fast.
	local initialized = {}
	for _, definition in order do
		local context = createContext(self, definition)
		self._contexts[definition.Name] = context
		if definition.Init then
			local ok, err = xpcall(definition.Init, traceback, definition, context)
			if not ok then
				-- The failing definition's own Cleanup is destroyed too.
				table.insert(initialized, definition)
				local stopErrors = teardown(self, initialized)
				local message = PREFIX .. ("Init failed for '%s': %s"):format(definition.Name, err)
				if #stopErrors > 0 then
					message ..= "\nWhile rolling back:\n" .. table.concat(stopErrors, "\n")
				end
				fail(self, message)
			end
		end
		table.insert(initialized, definition)
	end
	self._initialized = initialized

	-- Start: each on its own thread, in dependency order.
	for _, definition in order do
		if definition.Start then
			local context = self._contexts[definition.Name]
			local waits = definition.WaitForStart == true

			-- "Settled" means startup no longer waits on this definition: its
			-- Start returned, failed, timed out, or (without WaitForStart)
			-- yielded. Errors raised after settling go to OnError.
			local settled = false
			local failure: string? = nil
			local waiter: thread? = nil
			local function settle(err: string?): boolean
				if settled then
					return false
				end
				settled = true
				failure = err
				if waiter then
					resume(waiter)
				end
				return true
			end

			local startThread = task.spawn(function()
				local ok, err = xpcall(definition.Start, traceback, definition, context)
				if not settle(if ok then nil else err) and not ok then
					self._onError(PREFIX .. ("Start for '%s' failed after yielding: %s"):format(definition.Name, err))
				end
			end)
			self._startThreads[definition.Name] = startThread

			if not settled then
				if waits then
					local timeout = definition.StartTimeout or DEFAULT_START_TIMEOUT
					local timer = task.delay(timeout, function()
						if settled then
							return
						end
						-- Cancel the stuck Start before rolling back, so it can't
						-- keep running while its Stop and Cleanup execute.
						if coroutine.status(startThread) == "suspended" then
							pcall(task.cancel, startThread)
						end
						settle(("did not finish within %s seconds"):format(tostring(timeout)))
					end)
					waiter = coroutine.running()
					coroutine.yield()
					waiter = nil
					pcall(task.cancel, timer)
				else
					settle(nil)
				end
			end

			if failure then
				local stopErrors = teardown(self, initialized)
				local message = PREFIX .. ("Start failed for '%s': %s"):format(definition.Name, failure)
				if #stopErrors > 0 then
					message ..= "\nWhile rolling back:\n" .. table.concat(stopErrors, "\n")
				end
				fail(self, message)
			end
		end
	end

	self._state = "Running"
	self.Started:Fire()
	resumeWaiters(self, true, nil)
end

--- Yields until the app is running. Raises if startup failed.
function AppClass.AwaitStart(self: any)
	local state = self._state
	if state == "Running" or state == "Stopping" or state == "Stopped" then
		return
	end
	if state == "Failed" then
		error(PREFIX .. ("App '%s' failed to start: %s"):format(self.Name, tostring(self._failure)), 2)
	end
	table.insert(self._waiting, coroutine.running())
	local ok, message = coroutine.yield()
	if not ok then
		error(PREFIX .. ("App '%s' failed to start: %s"):format(self.Name, tostring(message)), 2)
	end
end

--- Stops every definition in reverse dependency order. Idempotent. Errors
--- from individual Stop calls are collected and raised after all have run.
function AppClass.Stop(self: any)
	local state = self._state
	if state == "Stopped" or state == "Stopping" or state == "Failed" then
		return
	end
	if state == "Starting" then
		error(PREFIX .. ("Cannot stop app '%s' while it is starting"):format(self.Name), 2)
	end
	if state == "Idle" then
		self._state = "Stopped"
		return
	end
	self._state = "Stopping"
	local errors = teardown(self, self._initialized)
	self._state = "Stopped"
	self.Stopped:Fire()
	if #errors > 0 then
		error(PREFIX .. ("App '%s' stopped with errors:\n%s"):format(self.Name, table.concat(errors, "\n")), 2)
	end
end

local App = {}

function App.new(options: AppOptions?): App
	if options ~= nil and type(options) ~= "table" then
		error(PREFIX .. "Options must be a table", 2)
	end
	local opts: AppOptions = options or {}
	local environment = opts.Environment
	if environment == nil then
		environment = detectEnvironment()
	elseif environment ~= "Server" and environment ~= "Client" then
		error(PREFIX .. 'Options.Environment must be "Server" or "Client"', 2)
	end
	if opts.OnError ~= nil and type(opts.OnError) ~= "function" then
		error(PREFIX .. "Options.OnError must be a function", 2)
	end
	local name = opts.Name or environment

	local self = setmetatable({
		Name = name,
		Environment = environment,
		Started = Signal.new(),
		Stopped = Signal.new(),
		_state = "Idle",
		_definitions = {},
		_byName = {},
		_contexts = {},
		_order = {},
		_initialized = {},
		_startThreads = {},
		_waiting = {},
		_failure = nil,
		_onError = opts.OnError or function(message: string)
			task.spawn(error, message, 0)
		end,
	}, AppClass)
	return (self :: any) :: App
end

--- Returns true if `value` is a Constella App.
function App.is(value: any): boolean
	return type(value) == "table" and getmetatable(value) == AppClass
end

return table.freeze({
	App = table.freeze(App),
})

local InsertService = game:GetService("InsertService")

local Package = script.Parent

local DEMO_PLACE = 2569622788
local MAIN_MODULE_ID = 1868400649
local MAIN_MODULE_NAME = "MainModule"

local AUTO_UPDATE = true
local LEGACY = false

local CONFIG = Package:FindFirstChild("Config")
local ADDONS = Package:FindFirstChild("Addons")
if CONFIG then
	local autoUpdate = CONFIG:GetAttribute("AutoUpdate")
	if autoUpdate ~= nil then
		AUTO_UPDATE = autoUpdate
	end
	local legacy = CONFIG:GetAttribute("Legacy")
	if legacy ~= nil then
		LEGACY = legacy
	else
		local legacyValue = CONFIG:FindFirstChild("Legacy")
		if legacyValue and legacyValue:IsA("ValueBase") then
			LEGACY = (legacyValue :: any).Value == true
		end
	end
end

do
	local ok, err = pcall(function()
		return script.Sandboxed
	end)
	if not ok and type(err) == "string" and string.find(err, "lacking capability") then
		error([[


[KOHL'S ADMIN PERMISSIONS FIX]

Select the Kohl's Admin folder in the Explorer and run this script in the command bar:

local obj = game.Selection:Get()[1]
for _, v in obj:GetDescendants() do v.Sandboxed = false end
while obj and obj ~= game do obj.Sandboxed = false obj = obj.Parent end

]])
	end
end

if not _G.KAU and not shared._K_LOADER_LOADED then
	_G.KAU = true
	shared._K_LOADER_LOADED = true
	shared._K_MODERN_LOADER = not LEGACY

	local legacyConfig = CONFIG and CONFIG:FindFirstChild("Legacy")

	if LEGACY then
		MAIN_MODULE_NAME = "MainModuleLegacy"
		if legacyConfig then
			for _, child in legacyConfig:GetChildren() do
				child.Parent = script
			end
		end
		script.Name = "Kohl's Admin Infinite"
		script.Parent = game:GetService("ServerScriptService")
	else
		Package.Parent = game:GetService("ServerScriptService")
	end
	AUTO_UPDATE = AUTO_UPDATE and game.PlaceId ~= DEMO_PLACE

	local localMainModule = script:FindFirstChild(MAIN_MODULE_NAME) or MAIN_MODULE_ID
	local localTools = script:FindFirstChild("Tools") or Package:FindFirstChild("Tools", true)

	if typeof(localMainModule) == "Instance" and localTools then
		local targetParent = localMainModule:FindFirstChild("Server") or localMainModule
		if not targetParent:FindFirstChild("Tools") then
			(if AUTO_UPDATE then localTools:Clone() else localTools).Parent = targetParent
		end
	end

	if not game:GetService("RunService"):IsStudio() then
		shared._KAI_TEST_HOOKS = nil
	end

	local ok, result = pcall(require, if AUTO_UPDATE then MAIN_MODULE_ID else localMainModule)

	if not ok then
		if AUTO_UPDATE then
			local function loadModuleAsset(assetId: number)
				local asset = InsertService:LoadAsset(assetId)
				local module = asset:FindFirstChild(MAIN_MODULE_NAME, true) or asset:FindFirstChild("MainModule", true)
				if module then
					if not LEGACY then
						local serverFolder = module:FindFirstChild("Server")
						if serverFolder and not serverFolder:FindFirstChild("Tools") then
							local tools = asset:FindFirstChild("Tools", true)
								or script:FindFirstChild("Tools")
								or Package:FindFirstChild("Tools", true)
							if tools then
								tools:Clone().Parent = serverFolder
							end
						end
					end
					return assert(require(module), ":LoadAsset() module returned invalid values!")
				end
				error(`Failed to find the source for {assetId}.`)
			end

			warn(
				"Kohl's Admin failed to auto-update from MainModule, trying to load from asset\nReason:\t"
					.. tostring(result)
			)
			ok, result = pcall(loadModuleAsset, 172732271)
			if not ok then
				warn(
					"Kohl's Admin failed to auto-update from asset, loading from local package\nReason:\t"
						.. tostring(result)
				)
				ok, result = pcall(require, localMainModule)
				if not ok then
					error(result)
				end
			end
		else
			warn("Kohl's Admin failed to load from local package\nReason:\t" .. tostring(result))
		end
	end

	if not LEGACY and ok and type(result) == "table" and type(result.initialize) == "function" then
		result.initialize(CONFIG, ADDONS)
	end
else
	warn(`Multiple Kohl's Admin models detected; removing duplicate at {Package:GetFullName()}`)
	Package:Destroy()
end

--!strict
--[=[
	Constella.Data.MemoryAdapter

	An in-memory backend for Studio testing and failure simulation. It is
	NOT persistent: everything is lost when the server stops.

	It models what Constella.Data relies on from a real backend:
	- session locking: one active session per key. A second server asking
	  for the same key takes it over; the first session saves, ends and is
	  told so (the same behaviour as ProfileStore's session stealing);
	- new keys start as a deep copy of the template;
	- failures: SimulateFailures makes the next N loads or saves fail.

	Several adapters can share one database to simulate several servers:
	```lua
	local database = MemoryAdapter.newDatabase()
	local serverA = MemoryAdapter.new({ Database = database })
	local serverB = MemoryAdapter.new({ Database = database })
	```
]=]

local Util = require(script.Parent.Util)

--- The in-memory storage behind one or more MemoryAdapters.
export type Database = { [string]: any }

export type Options = {
	--- Share one database between adapters to simulate several servers.
	Database: Database?,
	--- Seconds each load/save waits, to simulate network latency.
	Latency: number?,
}

--- A Data adapter (pass it as Config.Adapter) plus test helpers.
export type MemoryAdapter = {
	Open: (self: MemoryAdapter, name: string, template: { [any]: any }) -> Util.Backend,
	--- Makes the next `Loads` session starts and `Saves` saves fail.
	SimulateFailures: (self: MemoryAdapter, failures: { Loads: number?, Saves: number? }) -> (),
	--- A copy of the stored data for a key (nil if none).
	Peek: (self: MemoryAdapter, name: string, key: string) -> any,
	--- Stores data for a key directly, as if saved by an older game version.
	Write: (self: MemoryAdapter, name: string, key: string, data: any) -> (),
	--- Whether a live session currently owns the key.
	IsLocked: (self: MemoryAdapter, name: string, key: string) -> boolean,
}

local MAX_SAVE_ATTEMPTS = 3

local SessionClass = {}
SessionClass.__index = SessionClass

local function writeRecord(self: any): (boolean, string?)
	local adapter = self._backend._adapter
	if adapter._latency > 0 then
		task.wait(adapter._latency)
	end
	if adapter._failSaves > 0 then
		adapter._failSaves -= 1
		return false, "SaveFailed"
	end
	self._record.data = Util.deepCopy(self.Data)
	self._record.saves += 1
	return true
end

function SessionClass.IsActive(self: any): boolean
	return self._active
end

function SessionClass.OnSessionEnd(self: any, callback: () -> ())
	table.insert(self._endCallbacks, callback)
end

--- Saves now. Returns false and a reason if the save failed.
function SessionClass.Save(self: any): (boolean, string?)
	if not self._active then
		return false, "SessionEnded"
	end
	return writeRecord(self)
end

-- Saves (retrying), releases the lock and notifies listeners.
-- Returns false if the final save failed; the lock is still released so the
-- player can rejoin, and the stored data stays at the last good save.
local function finish(self: any): (boolean, string?)
	if not self._active then
		return true
	end
	self._active = false
	local saved, reason = false, nil
	for _ = 1, MAX_SAVE_ATTEMPTS do
		saved, reason = writeRecord(self)
		if saved then
			break
		end
	end
	if self._record.owner == self then
		self._record.owner = nil
	end
	for _, callback in self._endCallbacks do
		task.spawn(callback)
	end
	return saved, reason
end

function SessionClass.End(self: any): (boolean, string?)
	return finish(self)
end

local BackendClass = {}
BackendClass.__index = BackendClass

--- Starts a session for `key`. Yields. Returns nil and a reason on failure.
function BackendClass.StartSession(self: any, key: string, options: any): (any, string?)
	local adapter = self._adapter
	if adapter._latency > 0 then
		task.wait(adapter._latency)
	end
	local shouldCancel = options and options.ShouldCancel
	if shouldCancel and shouldCancel() then
		return nil, "Cancelled"
	end
	if adapter._failLoads > 0 then
		adapter._failLoads -= 1
		return nil, "Throttled"
	end

	local records = self._records
	local record = records[key]
	if record == nil then
		record = { data = Util.deepCopy(self._template), owner = nil, saves = 0 }
		records[key] = record
	end
	-- Session locking: take the key over from its current owner, which
	-- saves its latest data first.
	local owner = record.owner
	if owner ~= nil then
		finish(owner)
	end

	local session = setmetatable({
		Data = Util.deepCopy(record.data),
		_active = true,
		_record = record,
		_backend = self,
		_endCallbacks = {},
	}, SessionClass)
	record.owner = session
	return session
end

local AdapterClass = {}
AdapterClass.__index = AdapterClass

function AdapterClass.Open(self: any, name: string, template: { [any]: any }): any
	local database = self._database
	database[name] = database[name] or {}
	return setmetatable({
		_adapter = self,
		_records = database[name],
		_template = Util.deepCopy(template),
	}, BackendClass)
end

--- Makes the next `Loads` session starts and `Saves` saves fail.
function AdapterClass.SimulateFailures(self: any, failures: { Loads: number?, Saves: number? })
	self._failLoads = failures.Loads or 0
	self._failSaves = failures.Saves or 0
end

--- Test helper: a copy of the stored data for a key (nil if none).
function AdapterClass.Peek(self: any, name: string, key: string): any
	local records = self._database[name]
	local record = records and records[key]
	return if record then Util.deepCopy(record.data) else nil
end

--- Test helper: stores data for a key directly, as if saved by an older game version.
function AdapterClass.Write(self: any, name: string, key: string, data: any)
	local database = self._database
	database[name] = database[name] or {}
	database[name][key] = { data = Util.deepCopy(data), owner = nil, saves = 0 }
end

--- Test helper: whether a live session currently owns the key.
function AdapterClass.IsLocked(self: any, name: string, key: string): boolean
	local records = self._database[name]
	local record = records and records[key]
	return record ~= nil and record.owner ~= nil
end

local MemoryAdapter = {}

function MemoryAdapter.newDatabase(): Database
	return {}
end

function MemoryAdapter.new(options: Options?): MemoryAdapter
	local opts: Options = options or {}
	local adapter = setmetatable({
		_database = opts.Database or MemoryAdapter.newDatabase(),
		_latency = opts.Latency or 0,
		_failLoads = 0,
		_failSaves = 0,
	}, AdapterClass)
	return (adapter :: any) :: MemoryAdapter
end

return table.freeze(MemoryAdapter)

--!strict
--[=[
	Constella.Data.ProfileStoreAdapter

	Runs Constella.Data on top of ProfileStore (by loleris), which provides
	the DataStore persistence, session locking, autosaving, retries and
	shutdown handling. Constella adds migrations, reconciliation, player
	lifecycle handling and observability on top.

	```lua
	local ProfileStore = require(ServerScriptService.ProfileStore) -- you install it
	local store = Data.Store.new({
		Name = "PlayerData",
		Template = { Coins = 0 },
		Adapter = Data.ProfileStoreAdapter.new(ProfileStore),
	})
	```

	Verified against ProfileStore 1.0.3 (lm-loleris/profilestore) in its
	mock mode; see docs/Data.md for what has and has not been verified.

	Save completion
	ProfileStore's Profile:Save() and Profile:EndSession() return at once
	and write on a separate thread; OnSessionEnd even fires before the final
	write. This adapter therefore waits for ProfileStore's OnAfterSave
	signal (fired after a successful write) so that, in Constella:
	- profile:Save() returns true only once a save has been written;
	- store:Release(player) returns once the final save has been written;
	- store:Shutdown(budget) measures real save completion.
	Both waits are capped by SaveTimeout (default 30 seconds). On timeout
	they return false; ProfileStore keeps retrying the write in the
	background, and its own BindToClose handler keeps the server alive
	until pending saves finish.

	Mock mode
	Pass { Mock = true } to use ProfileStore's in-memory mock store. Use it
	for tests in places with DataStore access, so tests never touch real
	data. ProfileStore's mock StartSessionAsync ignores the Cancel callback.
]=]

local Util = require(script.Parent.Util)

export type Options = {
	--- Use ProfileStore's mock store (in memory, never touches real data).
	Mock: boolean?,
	--- Seconds to wait for a save or the final save to be written. Defaults to 30.
	SaveTimeout: number?,
}

local DEFAULT_SAVE_TIMEOUT = 30

-- Resumes the waiting caller unless it was cancelled while it waited.
local function resume(thread: thread)
	if coroutine.status(thread) == "suspended" then
		task.spawn(thread)
	end
end

-- Runs `trigger` (which starts a ProfileStore save) and waits until that
-- save has been written. ProfileStore fires OnSave synchronously when a
-- save starts and OnAfterSave after it is written, so the first
-- OnAfterSave after our OnSave marks completion.
local function saveAndWait(profile: any, trigger: () -> (), timeout: number): (boolean, string?)
	local started = false
	local written = false
	local timedOut = false
	local waiter: thread? = nil

	local onSave = profile.OnSave:Connect(function()
		started = true
	end)
	local onAfterSave = profile.OnAfterSave:Connect(function()
		if started and not written and not timedOut then
			written = true
			if waiter then
				resume(waiter)
			end
		end
	end)
	local function disconnect()
		onSave:Disconnect()
		onAfterSave:Disconnect()
	end

	local ok, err = pcall(trigger :: any)
	if not ok then
		disconnect()
		return false, tostring(err)
	end
	if not started then
		disconnect()
		return false, "SessionEnded"
	end

	if not written then
		waiter = coroutine.running()
		local timer = task.delay(timeout, function()
			if not written then
				timedOut = true
				resume(waiter :: thread)
			end
		end)
		coroutine.yield()
		waiter = nil
		pcall(task.cancel, timer)
	end
	disconnect()

	if timedOut then
		return false, "SaveTimeout"
	end
	return true
end

local SessionClass = {}
SessionClass.__index = SessionClass

function SessionClass.IsActive(self: any): boolean
	return self._profile:IsActive()
end

function SessionClass.OnSessionEnd(self: any, callback: () -> ())
	self._profile.OnSessionEnd:Connect(callback)
end

--- Saves now and yields until the save has been written (or SaveTimeout).
function SessionClass.Save(self: any): (boolean, string?)
	local profile = self._profile
	if not profile:IsActive() then
		return false, "SessionEnded"
	end
	return saveAndWait(profile, function()
		profile:Save()
	end, self._saveTimeout)
end

--- Ends the session and yields until the final save has been written
--- (or SaveTimeout). Returns true at once if the session already ended.
function SessionClass.End(self: any): (boolean, string?)
	local profile = self._profile
	if not profile:IsActive() then
		return true
	end
	return saveAndWait(profile, function()
		profile:EndSession()
	end, self._saveTimeout)
end

local BackendClass = {}
BackendClass.__index = BackendClass

function BackendClass.StartSession(self: any, key: string, options: any): (any, string?)
	local shouldCancel = options and options.ShouldCancel
	local profile = self._store:StartSessionAsync(key, {
		Cancel = shouldCancel,
	})
	if profile == nil then
		if shouldCancel and shouldCancel() then
			return nil, "Cancelled"
		end
		return nil, "SessionUnavailable"
	end
	if options and options.UserId then
		-- Associates the data with the user for GDPR / right-to-erasure requests.
		pcall(profile.AddUserId, profile, options.UserId)
	end
	local session = setmetatable({
		_profile = profile,
		_saveTimeout = self._saveTimeout,
	}, SessionClass) :: any
	-- Constella replaces the contents of this table in place, so ProfileStore
	-- keeps saving the same table it handed out.
	session.Data = profile.Data
	return session
end

local AdapterClass = {}
AdapterClass.__index = AdapterClass

function AdapterClass.Open(self: any, name: string, template: { [any]: any }): any
	local store = self._profileStore.New(name, template)
	if self._mock then
		store = store.Mock
	end
	return setmetatable({ _store = store, _saveTimeout = self._saveTimeout }, BackendClass)
end

local ProfileStoreAdapter = {}

--- `profileStoreModule` is the result of require(ProfileStore).
function ProfileStoreAdapter.new(profileStoreModule: any, options: Options?): Util.Adapter
	if type(profileStoreModule) ~= "table" or type(profileStoreModule.New) ~= "function" then
		error("[Constella.Data] ProfileStoreAdapter.new expects the ProfileStore module (require(ProfileStore))", 2)
	end
	local saveTimeout = if options and options.SaveTimeout ~= nil then options.SaveTimeout else DEFAULT_SAVE_TIMEOUT
	if type(saveTimeout) ~= "number" or not (saveTimeout > 0) or saveTimeout == math.huge then
		error("[Constella.Data] SaveTimeout must be a positive number of seconds", 2)
	end
	local adapter = setmetatable({
		_profileStore = profileStoreModule,
		_mock = options ~= nil and options.Mock == true,
		_saveTimeout = saveTimeout,
	}, AdapterClass)
	return (adapter :: any) :: Util.Adapter
end

return table.freeze(ProfileStoreAdapter)

const Players = game:GetService("Players")
const ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage")
const LocalPlayer = Players.LocalPlayer

const Crane = require(ReplicatedStorage.shared.packages.Crane)

const Character = Crane:CreateComponent({
	Name = "Character",
})

function Character.onStart(self: typeof(Character))
	self.Humanoid = self.instance:WaitForChild("Humanoid") :: Humanoid
	self.Root = self.instance:WaitForChild("HumanoidRootPart") :: BasePart
	self.Cleaner = Crane.Buttler.new()
	self.Tricks = {}
end

function Character:Destroy()
	self.Cleaner:Clean()
end

return Character

--!strict
--[=[
	Constella.Data.Store

	Player data on top of an adapter (ProfileStoreAdapter in production,
	MemoryAdapter for testing).

	Load pipeline (LoadAsync)
	1. Start a session through the adapter, retrying with backoff
	   (LoadAttempts, RetryDelay). Cancelled if the player leaves.
	2. Validate and migrate. Data without a version is version 0;
	   Migrations[n] upgrades version n to n+1. Migrations run on a copy.
	3. Reconcile: add template keys that are missing. Existing values are
	   never overwritten.
	4. Commit the migrated copy into the session and fire Loaded.

	Never overwrite on failure
	If any step fails - load, corrupt data, data from a NEWER game version,
	a missing or failing migration - the session is ended WITHOUT changing
	the stored data, the profile is not handed out, and (by default) the
	player is kicked. A player never plays on template data that could
	later be saved over their real data.

	Session loss
	If the backend ends a session (for example the player joined another
	server, which took the session over), the profile becomes inactive,
	writes through it raise, Released fires and the player is kicked if
	still here.
]=]

local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local RunService = game:GetService("RunService")

local Signal = require(script.Parent.Parent.Signal)
local Promise = require(script.Parent.Parent.Promise)
local Util = require(script.Parent.Util)

-- Type only: `typeof` in a type annotation isn't evaluated at runtime, so
-- Data still doesn't load Debug unless you pass it a logger.
type Logger = typeof(require(script.Parent.Parent.Debug).Logger.new(""))

--- What a Data backend provides. `Data.ProfileStoreAdapter` and
--- `Data.MemoryAdapter` both implement it; so can your own backend.
export type Adapter = Util.Adapter
--- One named store on a backend (what `Adapter:Open` returns).
export type Backend = Util.Backend
--- One player's stored data while this server holds it.
export type Session = Util.Session
export type SessionOptions = Util.SessionOptions

export type ErrorKind =
	"LoadFailed"
	| "PlayerLeft"
	| "Released"
	| "CorruptData"
	| "NewerVersion"
	| "MissingMigration"
	| "MigrationFailed"
	| "ShuttingDown"

export type DataError = {
	Kind: ErrorKind,
	Message: string,
}

--- `T` is the shape of a profile's data, taken from `Template`.
export type Config<T = { [string]: any }> = {
	--- Store name, passed to the adapter (DataStore name for ProfileStore).
	Name: string,
	--- Default data. New profiles start as a copy; old ones gain missing keys.
	--- Its type becomes the type of `profile.Data`.
	Template: T,
	--- Backend: Data.ProfileStoreAdapter.new(ProfileStore) or Data.MemoryAdapter.new().
	Adapter: Adapter,
	--- Current data version (integer >= 1). Defaults to 1.
	Version: number?,
	--- Migrations[n](data) upgrades version n to n+1. May mutate `data`
	--- or return a replacement table.
	Migrations: { [number]: (data: any) -> any }?,
	--- Session start attempts before giving up. Defaults to 3.
	LoadAttempts: number?,
	--- Seconds before the first retry; doubles each time. Defaults to 1.
	RetryDelay: number?,
	--- Kick players whose data cannot be loaded. Defaults to true.
	KickOnFailure: boolean?,
	--- Builds the storage key. Defaults to "Player_<UserId>".
	Key: ((player: Player) -> string)?,
	--- A Constella.Debug logger for load, release and error events.
	Logger: Logger?,
	OnError: ((message: string) -> ())?,
	--- Checks the data after migration and reconciliation, for example a
	--- Network.Check validator such as `Check.record({...})`. Returning
	--- false fails the load as CorruptData: the stored data is not changed
	--- and the player is kicked (with KickOnFailure).
	Validate: ((data: any) -> (boolean, string?))?,
	--- Check that every value written through Set, Update and Mutate can be
	--- saved to a DataStore, and raise at the write instead of failing at
	--- the next save. Off by default; `CheckWrites = RunService:IsStudio()`
	--- catches mistakes while testing at no cost in live servers.
	CheckWrites: boolean?,
}

--- Options for `profile:Mutate`.
export type MutateOptions = {
	--- Only these top-level keys are compared (and reported through
	--- Changed). Faster on large profiles; edits to other keys go unreported.
	Keys: { string }?,
}

--- A loaded player's data. `Data` has the type of the store's `Template`.
--- Read it freely; change it only with `Set` and `Update`.
export type Profile<T = { [string]: any }> = {
	Player: Player,
	Key: string,
	Data: T,
	Changed: Signal.Signal<string, any, any>,
	Get: (self: Profile<T>, key: string) -> any,
	Set: (self: Profile<T>, key: string, value: any) -> (),
	Update: (self: Profile<T>, key: string, updater: (current: any) -> any) -> (),
	--- Edits `Data` through a callback that receives it with its real type,
	--- then fires Changed for each top-level key that changed. A key holding
	--- a table counts as changed whenever it is compared (as with Update),
	--- so in-place edits are never missed.
	Mutate: (self: Profile<T>, mutator: (data: T) -> (), options: MutateOptions?) -> (),
	Save: (self: Profile<T>) -> boolean,
	IsActive: (self: Profile<T>) -> boolean,
	Release: (self: Profile<T>) -> (),
}

export type Stats = {
	Loaded: number,
	Loading: number,
	LoadsSucceeded: number,
	LoadsFailed: number,
	SessionsLost: number,
}

export type Store<T = { [string]: any }> = {
	Name: string,
	Loaded: Signal.Signal<Player, Profile<T>>,
	Released: Signal.Signal<Player>,
	--- Resolves with the profile, or rejects with a `DataError`.
	LoadAsync: (self: Store<T>, player: Player) -> Promise.Promise<Profile<T>>,
	Get: (self: Store<T>, player: Player) -> Profile<T>?,
	Release: (self: Store<T>, player: Player) -> (),
	BindPlayers: (self: Store<T>) -> (),
	Shutdown: (self: Store<T>, budgetSeconds: number?) -> boolean,
	GetStats: (self: Store<T>) -> Stats,
}

local PREFIX = "[Constella.Data] "
local VERSION_KEY = "_ConstellaVersion"
local DEFAULT_KICK_MESSAGE = "Your data could not be loaded. Please rejoin in a moment."
local SESSION_LOST_MESSAGE = "Your data was loaded on another server. Please rejoin."

-- Errors --------------------------------------------------------------------

local ErrorClass = {}
ErrorClass.__index = ErrorClass
ErrorClass.__tostring = function(self: any): string
	return ("%s%s: %s"):format(PREFIX, self.Kind, self.Message)
end

local function traceback(err: any): string
	return debug.traceback(tostring(err), 2)
end

local function dataError(kind: ErrorKind, message: string): DataError
	return (setmetatable({ Kind = kind, Message = message }, ErrorClass) :: any) :: DataError
end

local function isInGame(player: any): boolean
	return player.Parent ~= nil
end

-- Profile -------------------------------------------------------------------

local ProfileClass = {}
ProfileClass.__index = ProfileClass

local function checkActive(self: any, level: number)
	if not self._active then
		error(PREFIX .. ("The profile for %s is no longer active"):format(tostring(self.Key)), level)
	end
end

function ProfileClass.Get(self: any, key: string): any
	return self.Data[key]
end

-- Raises at the write if the value can't be saved. Callers check
-- `_checkWrites` first, so the default (off) costs one field read.
local function checkWrite(self: any, key: any, value: any, level: number)
	local problem = if type(key) ~= "string"
		then ("profile keys must be strings, got %s"):format(typeof(key))
		else Util.checkStorable(value, key)
	if problem then
		error(PREFIX .. ("Can't write to %s: %s"):format(tostring(self.Key), problem), level + 1)
	end
end

function ProfileClass.Set(self: any, key: string, value: any)
	checkActive(self, 3)
	local old = self.Data[key]
	if old == value then
		return
	end
	if self._store._checkWrites then
		checkWrite(self, key, value, 2)
	end
	self.Data[key] = value
	self.Changed:Fire(key, value, old)
end

--- Sets `key` to `updater(current)`. An updater may also change a table in
--- place and return it: Changed still fires (with the same table as new and
--- old value), so listeners never miss an edit made this way.
function ProfileClass.Update(self: any, key: string, updater: (any) -> any)
	checkActive(self, 3)
	if type(updater) ~= "function" then
		error(PREFIX .. "Update expects a function", 2)
	end
	local old = self.Data[key]
	local new = updater(old)
	-- The updater is user code and may have yielded past a session loss.
	checkActive(self, 3)
	if new == old and type(new) ~= "table" then
		return
	end
	if self._store._checkWrites then
		checkWrite(self, key, new, 2)
	end
	self.Data[key] = new
	self.Changed:Fire(key, new, old)
end

local function checkKeys(keys: any): boolean
	if type(keys) ~= "table" then
		return false
	end
	local count = 0
	for _, key in keys do
		count += 1
		if type(key) ~= "string" then
			return false
		end
	end
	return count == #keys
end

-- Queues Changed for one compared key, when its value differs or when it
-- holds a table that may have been edited in place. `changes` holds
-- (key, new, old) triples; new or old can be nil, so they're stored by
-- index (table.insert would skip a nil). Returns the new count.
local function report(key: any, new: any, old: any, changes: { any }, count: number): number
	if new ~= old or type(new) == "table" then
		changes[count + 1] = key
		changes[count + 2] = new
		changes[count + 3] = old
		return count + 3
	end
	return count
end

--- Edits Data through `mutator(data)`, which receives Data with its real
--- type, then fires Changed(key, new, old) for each top-level key that
--- changed: values that differ, keys that were added or removed, and every
--- compared key that holds a table (it may have been edited in place).
--- With `options.Keys`, only those keys are compared. If the mutator
--- raises, the changes it made are still reported, then the error is
--- re-raised. Don't yield in the mutator.
function ProfileClass.Mutate(self: any, mutator: (data: any) -> (), options: MutateOptions?)
	checkActive(self, 3)
	if type(mutator) ~= "function" then
		error(PREFIX .. "Mutate expects a function", 2)
	end
	local keys = if options ~= nil then options.Keys else nil
	if keys ~= nil and not checkKeys(keys) then
		error(PREFIX .. "Mutate Keys must be an array of strings", 2)
	end
	local data = self.Data
	-- One shallow copy (or one value per listed key) to compare against.
	local before: { [any]: any }
	if keys then
		before = table.create(#keys)
		for index, key in keys do
			before[index] = data[key]
		end
	else
		before = table.clone(data)
	end

	local ok, err = xpcall(mutator :: any, traceback, data)
	-- The mutator is user code and may have yielded past a session loss.
	checkActive(self, 3)

	local changes = {}
	local count = 0
	if keys then
		for index, key in keys do
			count = report(key, data[key], before[index], changes, count)
		end
	else
		for key, value in data do
			count = report(key, value, before[key], changes, count)
		end
		for key, old in before do
			if data[key] == nil then
				count = report(key, nil, old, changes, count)
			end
		end
	end
	-- The edits are already made in place, so listeners hear about them
	-- even when they can't be saved; the problem is raised afterwards.
	local problem: string? = nil
	if self._store._checkWrites then
		for index = 1, count, 3 do
			local key = changes[index]
			problem = if type(key) ~= "string"
				then ("profile keys must be strings, got %s"):format(typeof(key))
				else Util.checkStorable(changes[index + 1], key)
			if problem then
				break
			end
		end
	end
	local changed = self.Changed
	for index = 1, count, 3 do
		changed:Fire(changes[index], changes[index + 1], changes[index + 2])
	end
	if not ok then
		error(err, 0)
	end
	if problem then
		error(PREFIX .. ("Can't write to %s: %s"):format(tostring(self.Key), problem), 2)
	end
end

--- Requests a save now. Returns false if the session is gone or the save failed.
function ProfileClass.Save(self: any): boolean
	if not self._active then
		return false
	end
	local ok, saved, reason = pcall(self._session.Save, self._session)
	if not ok or not saved then
		self._store:_report(("Save failed for %s: %s"):format(self.Key, tostring(if ok then reason else saved)))
		return false
	end
	return true
end

function ProfileClass.IsActive(self: any): boolean
	return self._active
end

function ProfileClass.Release(self: any)
	self._store:Release(self.Player)
end

-- Store ---------------------------------------------------------------------

local StoreClass = {}
StoreClass.__index = StoreClass

function StoreClass._report(self: any, message: string)
	if self._logger then
		self._logger:Error(message, { Store = self.Name })
	end
	self._onError(PREFIX .. message)
end

function StoreClass._log(self: any, message: string, fields: { [string]: any }?)
	if self._logger then
		self._logger:Info(message, fields)
	end
end

-- Validates, migrates and reconciles the session data. Returns the
-- prepared copy, or nil and a DataError. Never touches session.Data.
function StoreClass._prepare(self: any, data: any): (any, DataError?)
	if type(data) ~= "table" then
		return nil, dataError("CorruptData", ("stored data is a %s, not a table"):format(typeof(data)))
	end
	local version = data[VERSION_KEY]
	if version == nil then
		version = 0
	end
	if type(version) ~= "number" or version % 1 ~= 0 or version < 0 then
		return nil, dataError("CorruptData", ("invalid stored version %s"):format(tostring(version)))
	end
	local target = self._version
	if version > target then
		return nil,
			dataError(
				"NewerVersion",
				("stored data is version %d but this server only understands up to %d"):format(version, target)
			)
	end

	local working = Util.deepCopy(data)
	while version < target do
		local migrate = self._migrations[version]
		if migrate == nil then
			return nil,
				dataError("MissingMigration", ("no migration from version %d to %d"):format(version, version + 1))
		end
		local ok, result = xpcall(migrate, function(err)
			return debug.traceback(tostring(err), 2)
		end, working)
		if not ok then
			return nil,
				dataError(
					"MigrationFailed",
					("migration %d -> %d failed: %s"):format(version, version + 1, tostring(result))
				)
		end
		if result ~= nil then
			if type(result) ~= "table" then
				return nil,
					dataError(
						"MigrationFailed",
						("migration %d -> %d returned a %s"):format(version, version + 1, typeof(result))
					)
			end
			working = result
		end
		version += 1
	end
	Util.reconcile(working, self._template)
	-- Validate sees the game's data only: Constella's version key is added
	-- afterwards, so validators like Check.record don't have to allow it.
	working[VERSION_KEY] = nil
	local validate = self._validate
	if validate then
		local ok, valid, reason = xpcall(validate, function(err)
			return debug.traceback(tostring(err), 2)
		end, working)
		if not ok then
			return nil, dataError("LoadFailed", ("Validate raised an error: %s"):format(tostring(valid)))
		end
		if valid ~= true then
			return nil, dataError("CorruptData", ("data failed Validate: %s"):format(tostring(reason or "invalid")))
		end
	end
	working[VERSION_KEY] = target
	return working
end

-- Ends a session (the adapter performs the final save, which may yield).
-- While it runs, the session is listed in `_ending`, so Shutdown also waits
-- for releases that started before it was called.
local function endSession(self: any, session: any, key: string)
	self._ending[session] = true
	local ok, saved, reason = pcall(session.End, session)
	self._ending[session] = nil
	if not ok or saved == false then
		self:_report(("Ending the session for %s failed: %s"):format(key, tostring(if ok then reason else saved)))
	end
end

local function kick(self: any, player: any, message: string)
	if self._kickOnFailure and isInGame(player) then
		pcall(player.Kick, player, message)
	end
end

local function onSessionLost(self: any, player: any, profile: any)
	if not profile._active then
		return
	end
	profile._active = false
	if self._profiles[player] == profile then
		self._profiles[player] = nil
	end
	self._stats.SessionsLost += 1
	self:_log("Session ended by the backend", { Key = profile.Key })
	profile.Changed:Destroy()
	self.Released:Fire(player)
	if isInGame(player) and not profile._releasing then
		kick(self, player, SESSION_LOST_MESSAGE)
	end
end

--- Loads (or returns the already loading/loaded) profile for `player`.
--- Returns a Promise that resolves with the Profile or rejects with a DataError.
function StoreClass.LoadAsync(self: any, player: Player): any
	if self._closing then
		return Promise.reject(dataError("ShuttingDown", "the store is shutting down"))
	end
	local loaded = self._profiles[player]
	if loaded then
		return Promise.resolve(loaded)
	end
	local loading = self._loading[player]
	if loading then
		return loading
	end

	local key = self._keyFor(player)
	-- The worker owns the session until it commits a profile. Cancelling the
	-- public promise must not cancel that worker or skip its final cleanup.
	local operation = { player = player, cancelled = false }
	self._pending[operation] = true

	local function shouldCancel(): boolean
		return self._closing or operation.cancelled or not isInGame(player)
	end

	local function cancelledError(): DataError
		local kind: ErrorKind = if self._closing
			then "ShuttingDown"
			elseif operation.cancelled and isInGame(player) then "Released"
			else "PlayerLeft"
		return dataError(kind, "loading was cancelled")
	end

	local resolve: (...any) -> (), reject: (...any) -> ()
	local promise: any
	promise = Promise.new(function(resolvePromise, rejectPromise, onCancel)
		resolve, reject = resolvePromise, rejectPromise
		onCancel(function()
			operation.cancelled = true
			if self._loading[player] == promise then
				self._loading[player] = nil
			end
		end)
	end)
	self._loading[player] = promise

	-- The worker starts once the public promise is in _loading, on a thread
	-- of its own. It's spawned, not deferred: a thread that loads profiles
	-- one after another (each Await resumed from the previous worker) would
	-- otherwise nest one deferral deeper per load and hit Roblox's limit of
	-- 80 after that many loads.
	task.spawn(function()
		local session: any = nil
		local committed = false
		local ok, profile, problem = xpcall(function(): (any, DataError?)
			if shouldCancel() then
				return nil, cancelledError()
			end
			local opened, result = Promise.retry(function()
				if shouldCancel() then
					return Promise.reject("Cancelled")
				end
				local acquired, reason = self._backend:StartSession(key, {
					UserId = (player :: any).UserId,
					ShouldCancel = shouldCancel,
				})
				return if acquired then acquired else Promise.reject(reason or "SessionUnavailable")
			end, {
				Attempts = self._attempts,
				Delay = self._retryDelay,
				Backoff = 2,
				ShouldRetry = function(reason)
					return reason ~= "Cancelled" and not shouldCancel()
				end,
			}):Await()
			if not opened then
				return nil,
					if shouldCancel()
						then cancelledError()
						else dataError("LoadFailed", ("could not start a session: %s"):format(tostring(result)))
			end
			session = result
			if shouldCancel() then
				return nil, cancelledError()
			end
			local prepared, failure = self:_prepare(session.Data)
			-- Migrations are user code and may yield for arbitrarily long.
			if shouldCancel() then
				return nil, cancelledError()
			end
			if not session:IsActive() then
				return nil, dataError("Released", "the session ended during loading")
			end
			if prepared == nil then
				return nil, failure
			end
			Util.replaceContents(session.Data, prepared)
			local loadedProfile = setmetatable({
				Player = player,
				Key = key,
				Data = session.Data,
				Changed = Signal.new(),
				_session = session,
				_store = self,
				_active = true,
				_releasing = false,
			}, ProfileClass)
			session:OnSessionEnd(function()
				onSessionLost(self, player, loadedProfile)
			end)
			self._profiles[player] = loadedProfile
			committed = true
			return loadedProfile, nil
		end, function(err)
			return dataError("LoadFailed", debug.traceback(tostring(err), 2))
		end)
		if session and not committed then
			endSession(self, session, key)
		end
		self._pending[operation] = nil
		if self._loading[player] == promise then
			self._loading[player] = nil
		end
		if not ok then
			problem, profile = profile, nil
		end
		if profile then
			self._stats.LoadsSucceeded += 1
			self:_log("Profile loaded", { Key = key })
			self.Loaded:Fire(player, profile)
			resolve(profile)
		else
			local kind = if type(problem) == "table" then problem.Kind else nil
			if not operation.cancelled and kind ~= "PlayerLeft" and kind ~= "ShuttingDown" and kind ~= "Released" then
				self._stats.LoadsFailed += 1
				self:_report(("Could not load %s: %s"):format(key, tostring(problem)))
				kick(self, player, self._kickMessage)
			end
			reject(problem)
		end
	end)
	return promise
end

function StoreClass.Get(self: any, player: Player): any
	return self._profiles[player]
end

--- Ends the player's session (the adapter performs the final save).
--- Cancels a load that is still in progress.
function StoreClass.Release(self: any, player: Player)
	for operation in self._pending do
		if operation.player == player then
			operation.cancelled = true
		end
	end
	local profile = self._profiles[player]
	if profile == nil then
		return
	end
	self._profiles[player] = nil
	profile._releasing = true
	profile._active = false
	endSession(self, profile._session, profile.Key)
	profile.Changed:Destroy()
	self:_log("Profile released", { Key = profile.Key })
	self.Released:Fire(player)
end

--- Loads players as they join and releases them as they leave.
function StoreClass.BindPlayers(self: any)
	if self._bound then
		return
	end
	self._bound = true
	local function load(player: Player)
		self:LoadAsync(player):Catch(function() end) -- failures are reported and handled by the store
	end
	table.insert(self._connections, Players.PlayerAdded:Connect(load))
	table.insert(
		self._connections,
		Players.PlayerRemoving:Connect(function(player)
			self:Release(player)
		end)
	)
	for _, player in Players:GetPlayers() do
		task.spawn(load, player)
	end
end

--- Stops new loads and releases every profile, waiting at most
--- `budgetSeconds` (default 20) for sessions to end. Sessions that were
--- already ending (for example a player who left just before the server
--- closed) are waited for too. Returns true if every session ended within
--- the budget. Call it from game:BindToClose.
function StoreClass.Shutdown(self: any, budgetSeconds: number?): boolean
	self._closing = true
	for _, connection in self._connections do
		connection:Disconnect()
	end
	table.clear(self._connections)

	local players = {}
	for player in self._profiles do
		table.insert(players, player)
	end
	for _, player in players do
		task.spawn(self.Release, self, player)
	end
	-- Every session being released, by this call or earlier, is in _ending
	-- until its final save has finished.
	local deadline = os.clock() + (budgetSeconds or 20)
	while (next(self._ending) ~= nil or next(self._pending) ~= nil) and os.clock() < deadline do
		task.wait()
	end
	local pending = 0
	for _ in self._ending do
		pending += 1
	end
	for _ in self._pending do
		pending += 1
	end
	if pending > 0 then
		self:_report(("Shutdown budget exceeded with %d pending load(s) or session end(s)"):format(pending))
		return false
	end
	return true
end

function StoreClass.GetStats(self: any): Stats
	local loading = 0
	for _ in self._pending do
		loading += 1
	end
	local loaded = 0
	for _ in self._profiles do
		loaded += 1
	end
	return {
		Loaded = loaded,
		Loading = loading,
		LoadsSucceeded = self._stats.LoadsSucceeded,
		LoadsFailed = self._stats.LoadsFailed,
		SessionsLost = self._stats.SessionsLost,
	}
end

local Store = {}

function Store.new<T>(config: Config<T>): Store<T>
	if RunService:IsRunning() and not RunService:IsServer() then
		error(PREFIX .. "Data.Store can only be used on the server", 2)
	end
	if type(config) ~= "table" then
		error(PREFIX .. "Store.new expects a config table", 2)
	end
	if type(config.Name) ~= "string" or config.Name == "" then
		error(PREFIX .. "Config.Name must be a non-empty string", 2)
	end
	if type(config.Template) ~= "table" then
		error(PREFIX .. "Config.Template must be a table", 2)
	end
	if config.Template[VERSION_KEY] ~= nil then
		error(PREFIX .. ("Config.Template must not contain the reserved key %s"):format(VERSION_KEY), 2)
	end
	if type(config.Adapter) ~= "table" or type(config.Adapter.Open) ~= "function" then
		error(PREFIX .. "Config.Adapter must be a Data adapter (ProfileStoreAdapter or MemoryAdapter)", 2)
	end
	local version = config.Version or 1
	if type(version) ~= "number" or version < 1 or version % 1 ~= 0 then
		error(PREFIX .. "Config.Version must be an integer >= 1", 2)
	end
	local migrations: { [any]: any } = config.Migrations or {}
	if type(migrations) ~= "table" then
		error(PREFIX .. "Config.Migrations must be a table", 2)
	end
	for from, migrate in migrations do
		if type(from) ~= "number" or from % 1 ~= 0 or from < 0 or from >= version then
			error(PREFIX .. ("Migration key %s must be an integer from 0 to %d"):format(tostring(from), version - 1), 2)
		end
		if type(migrate) ~= "function" then
			error(PREFIX .. ("Migrations[%d] must be a function"):format(from), 2)
		end
	end
	local attempts = config.LoadAttempts or 3
	if type(attempts) ~= "number" or attempts < 1 or attempts % 1 ~= 0 then
		error(PREFIX .. "Config.LoadAttempts must be a positive integer", 2)
	end
	local retryDelay = config.RetryDelay or 1
	if type(retryDelay) ~= "number" or retryDelay < 0 or retryDelay ~= retryDelay then
		error(PREFIX .. "Config.RetryDelay must be a non-negative number", 2)
	end
	if config.Key ~= nil and type(config.Key) ~= "function" then
		error(PREFIX .. "Config.Key must be a function", 2)
	end
	if config.Validate ~= nil and type(config.Validate) ~= "function" then
		error(PREFIX .. "Config.Validate must be a function", 2)
	end
	if config.CheckWrites ~= nil and type(config.CheckWrites) ~= "boolean" then
		error(PREFIX .. "Config.CheckWrites must be a boolean", 2)
	end

	-- New profiles start at the current version.
	local template = Util.deepCopy(config.Template)
	local adapterTemplate = Util.deepCopy(template)
	adapterTemplate[VERSION_KEY] = version

	local self = setmetatable({
		Name = config.Name,
		Loaded = Signal.new(),
		Released = Signal.new(),
		_backend = config.Adapter:Open(config.Name, adapterTemplate),
		_template = template,
		_version = version,
		_migrations = table.clone(migrations),
		_attempts = attempts,
		_retryDelay = retryDelay,
		_kickOnFailure = config.KickOnFailure ~= false,
		_kickMessage = DEFAULT_KICK_MESSAGE,
		_keyFor = config.Key or function(player: any): string
			return "Player_" .. tostring(player.UserId)
		end,
		_logger = config.Logger,
		_validate = config.Validate,
		_checkWrites = config.CheckWrites == true,
		_onError = config.OnError or function(message: string)
			task.spawn(error, message, 0)
		end,
		_profiles = {},
		_loading = {},
		_pending = {},
		_connections = {},
		_bound = false,
		_closing = false,
		_ending = {},
		_stats = { LoadsSucceeded = 0, LoadsFailed = 0, SessionsLost = 0 },
	}, StoreClass)
	return (self :: any) :: Store<T>
end

Store.VERSION_KEY = VERSION_KEY

--- True if `value` is a Data error, optionally of the given Kind.
function Store.isError(value: any, kind: ErrorKind?): boolean
	if type(value) ~= "table" or getmetatable(value) ~= ErrorClass then
		return false
	end
	return kind == nil or value.Kind == kind
end

return table.freeze(Store)
